contests.title: United States Representative, District 10

paragraphs: As a single dad who raised two sons and a former restaurant owner in the Bay Area, I understand the challenges families face making ends meet and building a secure future. I didn’t come to public service through ideology, but through real life—working union jobs, making payroll, and learning that listening and problem-solving matter more than slogans. That perspective has guided me through years of service as a mayor, councilmember, county supervisor, state legislator and now Congressman. My guiding principle is simple: I work for you. I’ve authored 73 pieces of legislation signed into law. I’ve helped over 15,000 residents resolve federal issues and held 272 town halls because accessibility and accountability are essential to effective representation. I’ve prioritized local projects that improve quality of life, including transportation and traffic relief, public safety investments, responsible infrastructure spending, and expanding access to mental health care—especially for children and families. I’ve worked to lower healthcare and housing costs, protect Social Security and Medicare, reduce gun violence, and fight to protect our air, water, and precious open space. At a time of growing division and dysfunction, I’ll defend democracy, uphold the rule of law, and restore trust in Congress through transparency, honesty and ethics to ensure our government remains accountable to the people—now and for future generations. I’m proud to be endorsed by U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla, former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, and local leaders across Contra Costa and Alameda Counties. I respectfully ask for your vote. Mark

contests.title: United States Representative, District 12

paragraphs: The Executive Branch is corrupt and overpowered. Costs are wildly out of control, and Al could reshape everything from jobs, to elections, to the future of our kids. We need a fresh, qualified candidate who understands both Al and the everyday struggles we face today. That’s why I am running. As a private citizen, I’ve been fighting for people for over a decade. I worked on an award-winning project for healthcare workers, negotiated with DOGE to spare a government agency, volunteer to support veterans telehealth, and have led teams that built technology to make democracy work better, from city hall to the federal government. Before that, I oversaw humanitarian, environmental, and climate projects in more than 20 countries, Government agencies have invited me to present, and top Al labs have recognized my work in making Al more accurate and aligned with what people want. I’m already meeting with Congress about my bill to rein in ICE, surveillance, Al, corruption, and dark money, and to fund electoral reform and release more Epstein Files. This earned me endorsement from several Epstein Survivors and a world-famous Al ethicist. If we want affordable living, healthcare, a corruption-free government, a clean environment, and a future safe for children, the elderly, immigrants, business owners, and LGBTQIA and BIPOC people, we need to not only stop losing ground, we need to fight back effectively. Status quo politics can’t even win yesterday’s battles, let alone win the future we want. But with your vote, we can win together. JamieJoyce.com CD12-1

For more than thirty years, I have led institutions across the Bay Area dedicated to lifting up our communities and delivering real change. Taking these lessons and the same mission to Congress, I have dedicated myself to delivering tangible change for the constituents of California’s 12th Congressional district. In my first term, I secured over $800 million in federal funding for the East Bay, including transformative resources that will improve public safety and increase access to housing and safe, reliable public transportation for my constituents. I have stood up to the Trump administration every single day: fighting against cuts to the health care and education programs my constituents rely on; holding the line on immigrant rights; and opposing endless wars. I have worked to release federal funds for community health centers that were illegally frozen by the Trump Administration, and fought to prevent the Administration from reducing SNAP benefits for kids and families. I have staunchly defended the rights of our immigrant communities by ensuring that constituents in need get casework assistance, and held the Administration accountable for its lawless immigration enforcement actions that have terrorized our communities. I will continue bringing resources home while advancing legislation that expands affordable housing, protects Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; strengthens public safety; champions disability justice; and ensures our region can thrive in the years and decades to come. This district is powerful, beautiful, and full of promise. I humbly ask for your vote. Learn more at LateefahSimon.com.

contests.title: United States Representative, District 14

paragraphs: I’ve been proud to call Alameda County home for three decades. My parents were migrant farm workers who sacrificed for a better way of life. Years later, I put myself through school while raising my own kids as a single mom. I know what it feels like to worry if we’ll make ends meet. We are now facing an unprecedented cost-of-living crisis. That’s why as the first Latina to serve as Mayor of Dublin, I worked to increase affordable housing and advance policies that created good-paying jobs. And we did – I proudly led Dublin to a “Best Places to Live” designation. Today, I fight for a stronger, healthier community as Director of Healthcare Services for an Alameda County Supervisor, where lowering healthcare costs and expanding access to vital services is my priority. This fight isn’t new to me. It’s what I’ve done my whole life. In Congress, I’ll fight for smart affordable housing solutions, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and lowering the cost of healthcare, childcare, and everyday items. This is why I am proudly supported by our firefighters and public safety officers, as well as working families, all Mayors and Alameda County Supervisors in our district, and dozens of local elected officials. I’d be honored to have your vote as well. Melissahernandez2026.com CD14-1

Families feel rising costs, uncertain paychecks, and extremist politics that distract from the real issues we all face. The greatest divide is not left versus right, but those at the top versus everyone working to get by. I’m running for Congress to get back to basics: food on the table, a roof over your head, well-paying jobs, quality healthcare, strong public schools, and an affordable life—so the American Dream is real again. For me, this is personal. After tragedy struck my family, I entered foster care before I was old enough to tie my own shoes. During the Great Recession, my family business tanked and our home was foreclosed. Working full-time, I paid my way through college, earned an MBA, and a Doctorate of Social Work from USC. After all of this, I’m still a renter hoping to buy my first home. I’m working to rebuild the American Dream for my family and all of us to have a fair shot. As your — State Senator, Mayor Pro Tempore, and Councilmember — I’ve made sure people come first in every budget and policy decision. Successfully, I capped insulin costs, secured $11 insulin pens, funded down payments for first-time homebuyers, supported small businesses, protected immigrants, renters, consumers, seniors, women and children, and expanded affordable housing. I’m proud to be supported by teachers, nurses, firefighters, police, and community leaders — including the sole endorsement of the California Democratic Party, Alameda County Sheriff Yesenia Sanchez, Superintendent Alysse Castro, Assemblymembers Ortega, Bonta, and Ransom, and Senators Wieckowski and Grayson. I’d be honored to earn your vote to rebuild the American Dream.

contests.title: United States Representative, District 17

paragraphs: For 26 years, the Bay Area has been my home. I raised my family, worked as an engineer, built a small business, and served our neighborhoods. I come from a middle-class family. I know the fear families feel when wages cannot keep pace with rent, groceries, utilities, insurance, and medical bills. I have struggled myself, and I understand the pain families carry. Congress should be public service, not a platform for ambition or building a national profile. My attention will remain on you: your affordability, safety, job, family, and future. Integrity comes first. I pledge not to buy or sell individual stocks while serving in Congress. I will support a stock-trading ban for members of Congress and their families. Public officials should serve people, not profit from their positions. I will fight to lower housing and healthcare costs, reduce prescription drug prices, strengthen Social Security, Medicare, protect coverage for preexisting conditions, and demand transparency from hospitals and insurers. As an engineer and technology leader, I will champion responsible innovation, support small businesses, protect American jobs, prepare workers for artificial intelligence, and create opportunities for graduates. I support voter identification, secure borders, and safe communities. I will work with Democrats, Republicans, and independents whenever it benefits our district. I will listen, remain accessible, return your calls, and judge every proposal by one standard: Does it improve your life? Our district deserves a fresh new voice. Give me two years to work for your family. I ask for your vote. www.tandonforcongress.com [email removed]

contests.title: State Senator, District 10

paragraphs: In the Navy, we live by a commitment to leave nobody behind. I believe our communities should live by these same words. That’s why I’ve dedicated my life to service as a Union City Councilmember, Navy Reserve officer, and housing leader. My grandparents were sent to Japanese-American internment camps during World War 2. Their history grounds my commitment to protecting immigrants across California being targeted by Trump and ICE. As a Vice-Mayor and County Housing Authority Chair, I’ve helped make it easier to build affordable housing, secured funding for homelessness services, expanded public transit, and supported renters. I’ve served in an intelligence role in the Navy Reserve and graduated from Harvard Law School. I’m also an elected Democratic Central Committee member and interned in the Obama White House. Today, my wife–a public school teacher and union member–and I are raising three kids. Our two oldest attend the same public school where my wife and I first met as kids. I feel a strong sense of duty to my family, community, and state. Californians are living without shelter, can’t afford groceries, make rent, or buy a home. We must do better. My platform: lower the cost of housing, utilities, and groceries; achieve universal healthcare and childcare; raise wages and protect workers; fully fund public schools; prepare communities for wildfire and climate threats; stop ICE; and protect our most vulnerable from Trump. Endorsements: California Democratic Party; California AAPI Legislative Caucus; Planned Parenthood Advocates Mar Monte; California Professional Firefighters; United Nurses Associations of California/Union of Health Care Professionals; California Environmental Voters; State Senator Aisha Wahab; Assemblymember Alex Lee; and Alameda County Supervisor Elisa Márquez. Let’s build a California with opportunity for all.

paragraphs: Everyone reading my message has a stake in the future of California. Your vote for me means you’ll have someone in the Assembly who will: Reject corporate and PAC contributions. Enact CalCare, affordable and first-rate health care that 86% of Californians want. A better healthcare system has been within our reach for years. Despite almost 16 years of one-party dominance in California, in each legislative session, compliant legislators have blocked CalCare. Champion the provision of housing for those most in need. Enable full transition of our energy grid to renewable energy. Transform oil refineries into operations that offer oil workers safe, green jobs. Block the plan for the Coal Port in Oakland. Establish progressive taxation so the wealthy pay their fair share. Provide free lifelong public education for everyone. Return ancestral lands to Indigenous Peoples and make reparations to Black American Freedman and Mexican American families robbed of their homelands. Repeal anti-BDS (Boycott Divestment Sanctions) laws and laws that prohibit educators from teaching about genocide anywhere in the world. Withhold our tax dollars from all corporations complicit in genocide. Shut down all ICE detention centers and not cooperate with ICE. I received a Masters degree in Education from UC Berkeley. A music teacher in the Oakland Unified School District for 29 years, I led an effort with parents and teachers to persuade the OUSD School Board to adopt an Integrated Pest Management Plan, thus banning pesticides on all OUSD properties. Visit my website, markrendon4ad14.com and vote for Mark Rendon! AD14-1

Since 2018, I’ve had the honor of representing the East Bay. Because of your support, working families are the only special interest I serve. That’s what gives me the courage to take on thorny problems and cast hard votes – because I know the East Bay cares more about the results I deliver than making special interest groups happy. I grew up in a mobile home in rural California, the daughter of two working-class parents. That home wasn’t much, but it allowed me to attend community college and eventually work in the Obama White House. Every family deserves that same foundation. California’s housing crisis must be solved. Over the past eight years, we’ve put real teeth in our housing law, streamlined permitting, and secured funding for affordable housing – tackling inertia and taking on entrenched interests to do so. But costs are still too high, homeownership is out of reach, and too many of our neighbors remain unhoused. If re-elected, I’ll continue to fight for our progressive values: driving down the cost of housing, taking on big tech to protect our kids online, cutting red tape holding back clean energy and wildfire resilience, defending reproductive freedom, and standing up to the Trump Administration’s lawlessness and cruelty. I do this work for my two daughters, for your family, and for everyone who calls the East Bay home. I’m proud to be endorsed by Attorney General Rob Bonta, SEIU California, California Professional Firefighters, and many others. I would be honored to have your vote.

paragraphs: It’s my honor to serve you in the Assembly. I’ve built a record of solving problems with commonsense solutions — fighting for our shared values and putting our community’s needs above special interests. I’m focused on issues that matter to local families — working across the aisle to make California more affordable, spending taxpayer dollars wisely, and investing in strong public schools. I’m fighting to lower PG&E bills and fix our insurance market. I’ve delivered critical dollars to our community for wildfire safety. I’m also protecting our environment by defending local open space and holding Big Tech accountable for data center energy and water use so you don’t pay for their power. I’ve worked with public safety officials to keep us safe by strengthening gun safety and hate crimes laws, and funding law enforcement response to organized retail theft. Recognizing the urgent mental health crisis, I helped create the 988 mental health emergency response system and increased the number of mental health professionals in California. I’ve led the fight for women’s health and reproductive choice by ensuring patients have affordable, safe, and comprehensive access to care from pregnancy and abortion care to menopause. And I’m keeping our kids safe online and ensuring AI technologies are used ethically and responsibly. I’ve passed legislation to safeguard children from digital exploitation, address mental health dangers from social media, and protect Californians who are victims of deepfakes. I humbly ask for your vote to continue this important work.

As a working mom of three who grew up experiencing poverty and housing insecurity, these issues are personal. Thanks to your support, we’ve expanded childcare, free school meals, and universal pre-K for thousands of children and established the California Legislative Children’s Caucus to ensure no child is hungry or left behind, while introducing new bills to reduce child poverty. As Assembly Health Committee Chair, I stand up to Big Corporations to lower prescription drug costs, ensure our seniors receive the home medical equipment they need, and strengthen neighborhood protections around coal facilities, protecting our clean air. And I’ve led legislation to clean up our streets, properly dispose of abandoned RVs, and ensure our neighborhoods are safe for all. We must continue to demand our fair share of funding to fight our homeless crisis and make affordable home ownership an achievable dream for all. That’s why I’ve fought for billions of dollars in state spending for housing creation, while expanding housing assistance for students and families, renter protections, and services to transition people off the street. I ask for your vote to continue to support our families in today’s economy and protect the health and safety of every Californian. Join me:

paragraphs: Our democracy and civil rights face the greatest threats in generations. As your Assemblymember, I’m taking bold action to ensure every family is protected, safe, and healthy in these troubling times. I authored multiple bills to end illegal raids against innocent residents, demand greater ICE oversight, and end benefits for private companies helping ICE. It is also getting even harder to afford housing and childcare, buy groceries, and access affordable healthcare in today’s tough economy. That’s why I authored/co-authored nearly 300 bills to help everyday people, including my legislation to save St. Rose Hospital— Hayward’s only emergency room—from closure. I sponsored legislation to stop big banks and credit card companies from charging businesses extra fees and provide tax relief for the small business owners who contribute to our community character and economy. And I continue to secure millions for East Bay and Tri-Valley programs to build more affordable housing; propose compassionate, effective solutions to homelessness; and protect clean, safe drinking water. Our free Diaper Drive now benefits more than 1,500 local families and infants. As Assembly Labor Committee Chair, I championed the largest corporate wage theft lawsuit and victory in California history—and will continue the fight to educate workers on their rights, ensure a Living Wage, and protect our firefighters and healthcare workers from the effects of toxic smoke. With your support, I can continue my leadership to protect your rights, make our dreams for homeownership possible for all, and keep healthcare services affordable and accessible. Thank you for your vote.

We all know the truth: it is becoming way too expensive to live in the Bay Area. Corporations and their billionaire executives have squeezed every tax break out of us taxpayers while profiting from skyrocketing rents, home prices, and essential goods. I’ve been consistently leading the fight to tax the rich and fight against corporate greed. Since day one, I have rejected all campaign contributions from corporations because I am accountable to you, not the corporate interests. Above all else, I believe in the integrity of our democracy – that the government should serve all people, not the rich and powerful. I’m running for re-election to continue the fight against a fascist federal regime, fix the housing crisis, and rein in corporate greed. Humbly, I ask for your vote to continue representing you. www.VoteAlexLee.com / instagram/twitter: alex_lee / [email removed]

paragraphs: It has been a privilege to serve as your Trustee on the Ohlone Community College District Board for the past eight years. I believe higher education must deliver the training, network, and support students need to build strong careers, achieve financial stability, and reach their full potential. At Ohlone, our commitment to student success has resulted in increased enrollment, stellar transfer rates to four-year colleges and universities, and outstanding certificate training in Advanced Manufacturing, Biotechnology, Cybersecurity, Business, and Healthcare—specifically designed to transition students directly into high-demand jobs. Amid decreasing federal funding, experienced leadership is essential. As President of the California Community College Trustees Board in 2026, I fiercely advocated for statewide policies supporting 2.2 million students—always putting student success, opportunity, and basic needs such as mental wellness support, food security, and affordable housing at the center of our mission. With your vote, I will continue my dedicated work of “Putting Students First” to ensure accessible, high-quality education for our entire community. Thank You for your Trust and Support. https://www.ohlone.edu/board-trustees/board-members/sue-chan

I’m a mother, veterinarian, small business owner, nonprofit founder, and Alameda County Commissioner on the Status of Women. I raised three children in Fremont, and two attended Ohlone College. I understand the value of accessible, quality education and budgeting for those you care about. I made history as the first woman president of a Veterinary organization and strengthened it. As a Rotary District Chair, I connect students with professionals and career opportunities. Through my nonprofit, I support programs fighting human trafficking and providing cleft lip and palate surgeries. We built Ohlone. We fund it. And too many of our neighbors never set foot on campus. Students First. Expand access to required classes, strengthen academic counseling and mental health services, and offer schedules that work for students balancing jobs and families. Open Ohlone’s doors wider. Expand short-term programs for working adults, career-changers and lifelong learners. Train for jobs that are here. Ohlone should prepare residents for local careers through stackable certificates built with employers who are hiring. Spend like it’s your money. Every major expense explained in plain language, in public, before the vote. I’m not a career politician. Fresh energy. Practical leadership. Students first. See my endorsements at soniasalwan.com CANDIDATE 4 STATEMENTS

paragraphs: I am a Certified Public Accountant, parent of Alameda Unified School District graduates, and longtime Alameda school volunteer with 20 years of service to Alameda Unified School District. I have served as PTA Treasurer, School Site Council member, and chair of the Alameda Unified School District Parcel Tax Oversight Committee. Professionally, I have more than 25 years of experience in strategic financial planning, budgeting, audits, and financial accountability as a nonprofit Chief Financial Officer, including leadership in affordable housing organizations. As a school board member, my priorities are excellent academic outcomes 4 for every student, responsible budgeting that puts classrooms first, supporting and retaining excellent teachers, safe and welcoming schools, and transparent communication with families and the community. I believe students learn best when schools provide high academic expectations, early support for struggling learners, and opportunities for every child to succeed. I am committed to asking thoughtful questions, listening to families and educators, making data-informed decisions, and ensuring taxpayer dollars are managed responsibly. I have built my career on integrity, collaboration, and accountability. I will bring financial expertise, thoughtful leadership, and a proven record of community service to help Alameda Unified School District provide an excellent education for every student.

I am honored to serve on the Alameda Unified School District Board of Education because I believe every child deserves an excellent education that prepares them for college, careers, and a fulfilling life. I am proud to put my 25 years of education policy and fiscal expertise to work for the community my family calls home and where my children have attended school. I hold a master’s degree from Harvard Graduate School of Education, and my professional career has focused on strengthening public schools and improving outcomes, particularly for historically underserved students. I previously served as Co-Executive Director of a California-based education advocacy organization, and today, as a Partner with a leading national nonprofit, I help education leaders develop data-driven policies and strategies that support student success. Here in Alameda, I have served as a School Site Council member, chaired the district’s Parcel Tax Oversight Committee, and now serve as an AUSD Trustee. As your board member, I helped secure a 10% pay increase and more affordable health benefits for our educators and staff while advancing a plan for long-term fiscal sustainability. I have also worked to raise academic expectations and expand opportunities for all students. I would be honored to earn your vote and continue serving Alameda’s students, families, and schools.

statement.designation: Trustee – Alameda Unified School District, Retired Accounting Professor, Retired Non-Profit Co-founder for a Local Basketball Club
paragraphs: Since joining the AUSD Board, I have actively sought the input of our students, teachers, staff, parents, and community members to meet the challenge of providing our children with the highest quality education. Recognizing the importance of preparing our students to be college and career ready, I established a joint subcommittee between AUSD and Peralta Community College to strengthen our collaboration in offering free services directly to our students. The board has worked closely with stakeholders to pass multiple parcel taxes and facility bonds, ensuring Alameda remains a destination district that retains and attracts excellent teachers and staff. While other districts have suffered staff reductions and budget cuts, our district achieved a three-year labor agreement with our certificated and classified staff—a remarkable accomplishment that reflects the positive, productive working relationships between the board and our labor partners. As a proud Asian-American Alamedan, I attended Otis Elementary School, Lincoln Middle School, and both Alameda High School and Encinal High School. I have earned Accounting, Finance, and Business degrees from the University of California, Berkeley, and Arizona State University. Currently, I serve on the Community of Harbor Bay Isle board, representing my neighborhood. It has been a genuine privilege to serve as your trustee these past four years, and I respectfully ask for your vote. www.gary4alamedakids.com ALUSDG-1

Artificial intelligence is reshaping public education, bringing tremendous opportunities and legitimate concerns. As a former Alameda Board of Education member for 12 years, I believe AI should be governed thoughtfully so our students benefit from personalized learning while schools protect privacy, promote equity, preserve meaningful human relationships, and teach responsible AI use. Technology should empower great teachers—not replace them—and every decision should put students, educators, and families first. As a 45-year Alameda resident, I understand our community’s values, traditions, and educational priorities. My son and two daughters graduated from Alameda public schools, and today five of my grandchildren are continuing that tradition. I want every Alameda student to have the same opportunities my own family has enjoyed through our public schools. Strong schools begin with excellent teachers, responsible governance, and meaningful partnerships with families. Together, we can ensure Alameda’s schools continue to prepare every student to thrive in a rapidly changing world. I would be honored to earn your trust and your vote.

As a parent, community organizer, Peralta College certified Early Childhood Educator (ECE), special needs nanny, and disability rights advocate, I have dedicated my life to serving children and their families. I have one child who graduated from AUSD with an IEP, and another currently enrolled with a 504 Plan. As a former wheelchair youth athlete, I experienced firsthand the challenges many students and families continue to face today. At age 15, I became the lead plaintiff in Putnam v. Oakland Unified School District, by permanently establishing accessibility as a fundamental civil rights issue while uncovering systemic multimillion-dollar bond misappropriation. I will advocate for strong education services for all, accessible learning environments, responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars, and transparent, accountable decision-making. Our educators deserve the resources and support they need to help every student succeed. As your trustee, I will be your advocate. I will demand independent financial audits of bond allocations, prioritize basic classroom safety, support competitive teacher compensation, and firmly reject campus hate speech. We must invest in every student and educator, so families want to stay and return to Alameda. I respectfully ask for your vote to ensure true public service.

paragraphs: I am proud to submit my candidacy for Castro Valley Unified School District, School Board Trustee. I am a father of three students in the district, I served on the Executive Board for Castro Valley Elementary’s Parent and Teacher Association and I am a member, and former president of the Citizens Advisory Committee for the Hayward Area Recreation and Park District. In my work as president, I advised the Board of Directors on district operations and the development of recreation programs. For almost two decades, I have served as a Peace Officer and Public Information Officer in unincorporated Alameda County. As a Public Information Officer, I developed long standing relationships with community groups, key stakeholders, families, students, and educators. These relationships have been and always will be rooted in trust, transparency, and effective communication. If elected I will strive to ensure our schools are safe and equitable for everyone. I will work hard to improve our students’ quality of learning and access to advanced placement classes, and I will support teachers and collaborate with our local safety partners. A vote for me is a vote for safe campuses, educational excellence, and accountability.

Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed. That belief is why I am running for the Castro Valley Unified School District Board of Education. As a proud product of public education, a parent, a Financial Leader, and a proud Trustee Area 3 resident for more than twenty years, I understand that strong schools are built through responsible leadership, fiscal stewardship, collaboration, and trust. My husband and I chose Castro Valley because of its outstanding schools and strong sense of community. Today, our son is a proud graduate of Castro Valley Unified, and our daughter continues her education in the district. As your Trustee, I will listen to students, families, educators, staff, and our community. I will work to improve student achievement, strengthen reading and math proficiency, support safe and inclusive schools, and ensure taxpayer dollars are invested wisely, transparently, and responsibly. Every decision I make will begin with one simple question: Will this improve outcomes for students? Together, we can build on Castro Valley’s tradition of excellence and create even greater opportunities for every student. Because every child deserves the opportunity to succeed. I would appreciate your support on this journey. Together we can make the possible happen.

Our public schools are going through some tough times right now. With several Board members leaving, we have a great chance to bring in strong new leaders, fresh ideas, and a big focus on students and families. I have worked for 35 years as a licensed California Certified Public Accountant. Now I want to help in an even more important way—making sure our schools stay strong, exciting, and always focused on helping kids succeed. School money comes mostly from how many students attend. When fewer kids come, the schools get less money. Castro Valley schools have stayed strong because families choose us—including many 4 families who live outside our district. We must keep earning that trust! As a Board member, I will be honest, speak the truth, and really listen to parents. I will help make sure our schools are kind places with no bias or unfair treatment. We will work hard to help all students do better without making standards easier. This election is very important for our schools’ future. If you want caring, professional leaders who get results, please vote for me. Together, we can build strong schools and a bright future for our kids!

I bring a parent’s perspective, diverse representation, and accountable leadership to the Board. I am the daughter of a community college science professor, Five Canyons homeowner since 2007, California public school and UCSD graduate, and parent of two CVUSD students. I speak English, Cantonese, and Mandarin. My deep commitment to our schools is proven by my extensive volunteer work. I have served our schools as Independent Elementary PTA Treasurer, School Site Council member, CV Booklegger, FAME Coordinator, and have supported the CV Education Foundation, CVHS FIRST Robotics Team, CVHS Athletic Boosters, and secured community sponsorships for programs like the CVHS Marching Band. I will focus on measurable progress in literacy, math, student well-being, and college and career readiness, while supporting rigorous academics, expanded learning opportunities, and a safe school culture. Every student—from TK, SpEd, to adult school—deserves rigorous academics, a safe school culture, and support to succeed. I will prioritize resources that benefit students, evaluate programs based on results, and support sustainable strategies to attract and retain excellent educators. I am committed to listening, collaborating, and making thoughtful, student-centered decisions for every family in our district. I ask for your support and vote on November 3.

contests.title: Castro Valley Unified School District Governing Board Member, Area 4

paragraphs: I am running for the Castro Valley Unified School District Board, District 4, because I believe strong schools are built through trust, communication, and community. For 14 years, Castro Valley has been home. My husband and I are raising three children who attended CVUSD schools from elementary through high school. I have experienced our district as a parent, volunteer, parent club leader, booster secretary, and classified substitute. I earned a bachelor’s degree in speech communications from the University of Wisconsin Whitewater. I have also held leadership positions at all the schools my kids have attended, and was honored as CVUSD Volunteer of the Year for Creekside Middle School. I want to be a bridge between our community and schools. I want to listen to our families, support our teachers and staff, and collaborate with district leadership. I believe in transparency, respect, and accountability. My priorities include safe schools that are well-maintained, student mental health, responsible facilities planning, and strong communication. I believe that every student deserves a meaningful path after graduation. We should value trades, apprenticeships, career training, the arts, and college degrees equally, by providing visible, accessible, and fully supported pathways to success for all students. If these ideas resonate with you, I hope you’ll support me.

If you want to raise academic standards, if you want more Advanced Placement (AP) classes, and if you want to end 50% credit for doing no work, then vote Brian A. Foster to the CVUSD School Board, Area #4. County statistics currently place Castro Valley’s academic performance squarely in the middle of our county. We can and should compete academically with high-performing school districts like Dublin, Pleasanton, and Fremont. Join me in restoring Castro Valley’s schools to excellence and making academic achievement our #1 priority. My 13 years as a social studies teacher and 30 years in public sector management provide a unique combination of skills and experience necessary to demand academic excellence. Together, we will raise academic standards and celebrate real student success. You deserve honest feedback on your children’s academic progress and preparation for college-level rigor. I will ensure that our teachers have the opportunity, authority, and support necessary to provide your children with the best education possible. Real learning happens in the classroom, so let’s keep the focus there. I am supported by a wide variety of community leaders who recognize my commitment to fighting for an honest education. Please visit my website for more information on my positions and endorsements:

Our schools are at a turning point. With several Board members leaving, we have a real opportunity to bring in stronger leadership, fresh ideas, and a clear focus on students and families. I’ve spent my career as a scientist at our national laboratories in Livermore and Berkeley, solving complex problems. Now I’m stepping forward to take on one that matters even more—ensuring our schools stay strong, competitive, and focused on student success. School funding depends largely on student attendance. When enrollment declines, resources shrink. Castro Valley has remained strong because families choose our schools, including many from outside the district. That choice is not guaranteed—we have to earn it by maintaining high standards, safe campuses, and strong academic programs. As a Board member, I will tell you the truth, listen to parents, expand access to Advanced Placement courses, ensure our schools are free from bullying, and raise achievement without lowering standards. This election will decide the direction of our schools. If you want leadership that is honest, focused, and committed to results, I ask for your vote. Let’s choose strong schools and a stronger future—together.

I am running because I believe every child deserves a safe, supportive, and inspiring learning environment where they can reach their full potential. Our schools lay the foundation for our children’s future, and every student should have access to a high-quality education that prepares them for success in life. I believe every decision should put students’ well-being first. I am committed to providing transparent, accountable, and responsive leadership. My experience as a paraprofessional and student advocate inspired me to expand my support for students beyond a single school. I am running for the Dublin Unified School District Board, Trustee Area 3, because I saw firsthand how dedicated teachers and engaged families can make a lasting difference in a student’s education. I also witnessed the challenges our schools face and the importance of having board members who listen, collaborate, and make thoughtful decisions in students’ best interests. I will work to ensure every student has the opportunity to reach their full potential while preserving the high standard of education our community expects.

paragraphs: I am a parent of an eighth grader in Dublin Unified School District and a rising college freshman. Amazing public schools attracted my family to Dublin, and for years, I have worked alongside parents, educators, staff, and district leaders to give back. I served two years as President of the Kolb Elementary School Parent-Faculty Club and I am entering my third year as Vice President of the Fallon Middle School Parent-Faculty Club. Across both roles, I worked hard to give parents a real voice and support our teachers’ needs. I also engage directly and deeply with our Dublin Unified community, volunteering as a room parent, organizing dozens of outreach events, and fundraising for various classroom resources and local nonprofits. I also chaired the Citizens Bond Oversight Committee, and served on the Parcel Tax Oversight Committee, ensuring that our tax dollars are responsibly spent, and that our students have the best resources and facilities possible. Dublin Unified has gone through many challenges lately. We deserve leadership that will show up, listen closely, and work hard so every student will succeed. As your School Board Trustee, I will bring hands-on experience, responsible fiscal oversight, and a parent-centered approach. Together, let’s move Dublin Unified forward.

My qualifications to be your Trustee are apparent in my voting record. I consistently advocated and voted for a second high school. Completing Emerald HS has been the main focus of my time in office. There is still much to do; making sure EHS has room for student parking, which the DUSD Board committed to in the Project EIR, rather than intruding into neighborhoods around the school. When I started on the Board, DUSD had over $20 million in discretionary reserves. The majority of that money has been spent over the consistent objections of eastside Board Members. Deficit spending continues to occur, managed only by deferring much needed maintenance. Prior to being elected to the Board, I campaigned against Measure E, a bond used to purchase computers that are already obsolete and no longer in use. Regardless, we will continue to pay that money off for the next 19 years. Hard choices will have to be made to restore a financially sound School District. It has been my privilege and honor to advocate for our schools by supporting financial decisions focused on future solvency. Your vote is appreciated. Thank you!

paragraphs: Every decision our School Board makes should begin with one question: How does this help students? This principle will guide every vote I cast. I am the parent of two Hayward Unified School District students and a Research Director with a Master of Science in Biostatistics from California State University, East Bay, and a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics with an emphasis in Statistics and a minor in Business. My goal is to help every child feel safe, supported, and prepared for success. I would be honored to earn your vote. Visit www.michelle4husd.com.

Serving as a strong voice for families, I have served on the School Usage Design Team, School Site Council, Site-Based Decision Making Committee, and District Advisory Committee. Active parent involvement is essential for our schools to thrive. Real change begins with total accountability. To help our children succeed, we must hold leadership responsible and make students our number one priority. I will fight for all students, especially our Special Education students, by supporting early evaluations, inclusive learning opportunities, data-driven programming, safe environments, and direct student funding. I will listen, discuss, and act through respectful, truthful partnerships with parents, teachers, and administrators. Every student deserves a high-quality education to compete globally. paragraphs: As a Mama to two elementary aged students at Junction K8, I will work with our new Superintendent and fellow Trustees to center transparency, respect, and accountability in setting our district’s priorities. With my education (BA in Economics and Political Science; MBA) and career as an expert in finance operations, advising my dozens of clients in reorganizing, evaluating and deploying the best solutions to solve their problems, I fill a critical skill gap on our Board. Alongside administration, staff, and bargaining units, my participation in financial matters will balance both the short and long term fiscal health. Together, we will once again be the district attracting and retaining talent and will elevate our students to the next level. I humbly ask for your vote this November!

I believe every voice in our community deserves to be heard. Parents, teachers, students, administrators, and community members all bring valuable perspectives, and effective leadership starts with listening. Our children are growing up in an increasingly connected and, at times, turbulent world. Schools should be places where students can focus on learning, developing confidence, building meaningful relationships, and preparing for their futures without unnecessary distractions. As your Area 2 representative, I will listen, ask questions, work collaboratively, and keep students at the center of every decision. I am committed to supporting our teachers, engaging our families, and helping ensure that every student has the opportunity to succeed. I would be honored to serve our community.

paragraphs: As a Livermore mother of two elementary students and an aunt to many children in our District, practicing chiropractor, small-business owner, and current LVJUSD Board Member, I am running for re-election because our kids deserve better. I have lived here nearly 15 years. In 2024 I earned the most votes of any candidate despite heavy special-interest opposition. I am the only board member who has earned a Master’s in Governance through the California School Boards Association and have completed the Livermore Leadership Program. I have been the consistent voice for academic excellence, campus safety, and fiscal responsibility. I serve on our schools’ PTA, the Little League Board, and my church’s Children’s Ministry. I regularly visit schools, work alongside teachers & staff on the Math Task Force, and cheer students on at sports, music, STEAM events, and Special Olympics. My husband and I donate our time and resources to schools, troops, sports teams, nonprofits, and individual students needing support. I will keep working to keep girls safe in their sports and private spaces, strengthen reading and math, and put students first—not ideology. I am the only candidate who has already stood firm under pressure. With your support I will continue this work through 2030. I would be honored to have your vote.

statement.designation: General Contractor and Small Business Owner
paragraphs: My daughter is a sophomore at Livermore High. That’s why I’m running. I’m a builder, not a politician. For thirteen years I ran construction and facilities operations, most recently as Director of Operations and Production, managing crews and budgets where going over wasn’t an option. I hold a California General Contractor’s license. I know what deferred maintenance actually costs, what a fair contract looks like, and how to spot a padded bid. Our district spends serious money on facilities, bonds, and vendor contracts. That’s your money. I’ll read every line of it. My priorities are common sense: dollars in the classroom and in front of teachers, campuses that are safe and well maintained, and a budget any parent can actually understand. Trades and career pathways for the kids who aren’t headed to a four-year school — because we need electricians and welders as much as we need engineers. I’m a small business owner. I make payroll. I earn trust one commitment at a time. I’ll show up, ask hard questions, and give you a straight answer even when it isn’t the popular one. I’d be honored to earn your vote.

candidates.name: Christiaan Vandenheuvel
candidates.designation: Member, Board of Education, Livermore Valley Joint Unified School District

paragraphs: I currently serve on the Livermore Valley Joint Unified School District Board of Trustees and am running for the Area 5 seat to continue that work. I immigrated to the United States at age twenty and learned English as a second language, which informs how I see every student’s potential. I served three years as PTSA president at Livermore High School and on the School Site Council there and at East Avenue Middle School. As the spouse of a high school teacher, the father of a current student and two district graduates, I am invested in our schools every day. My work on the board is grounded in good data, steady and pragmatic judgment, and a collaborative culture that keeps the focus on students. My priorities are strengthening education quality and results, supporting innovative teaching, and making sure every student, regardless of background, has what they need to succeed. I will keep showing up as a reasonable, practical voice for students, educators, and parents. I would appreciate your vote to continue this work.

statement.designation: Professor, New Haven Unified School District Trustee
paragraphs: As your New Haven Unified School District Trustee, I respectfully ask for your vote for re-election. As a parent of three children who have all been educated in New Haven schools and a tenured Professor of Physics at Mission College with over 24 years of experience in public education, I have dedicated my career to helping students succeed. Before being elected, I volunteered in our schools for more than a decade through Art Vistas, Chess Club, STEM programs, and other youth organizations. As your trustee, I have focused on expanding educational opportunities, strengthening student achievement, and being a thoughtful steward of taxpayer dollars. During my first term, I championed expanding opportunities for students by advancing middle school Spanish, Speech & Debate, and Math Olympiad; strengthening college pathways through our California State University, East Bay partnership; and improving school safety and traffic flow. I have remained accessible through my regular Chat With Your Trustee office hours, school visits, and community engagement because I believe the best decisions are made by listening to our community. Every decision I make is guided by one question: What is best for students? I would be honored to earn your vote and continue serving our community.

I am a neighbor who is a product of the New Haven Unified School District. I attended Elementary through High School at NHUSD and University at San Jose State. My son now is in Elementary at NHUSD and this mission is personal in keeping the district progressing forward. I built a career as a software engineer at Google and Salesforce before launching my own businesses over the past three years. Now pursuing my Master’s in Computer Science at Georgia Tech online program, I bring a unique blend of technical expertise in STEAM, problem-solving, entrepreneurship, and leadership to our school board. I understand our district’s unique strengths and the real-world skills our children need to succeed. Our teachers are the foundation of our district, and they are the ones that have shaped my experience. I am deeply grateful for their dedication, care, and expertise they bring to our classrooms every single day. My priorities are rooted in the core values of: Honesty, putting students first, listening to parents, empowering our teachers, driving increased resources to our schools and community integrity. I respectfully ask for your vote to serve our community.

As a software engineer with 20 years of experience, a father of a student in the New Haven Unified School District, and the husband of a teacher in NHUSD, I see our schools through the eyes of both a parent and a partner in education. I’m running for School Board Trustee because every child deserves classrooms that prepare them for a changing world—and every teacher deserves the support to make that possible. Technology is reshaping how we live and work. AI, robotics, and digital tools are no longer optional; they are essential. I want to bring practical technology into our schools so students gain needed skills and teachers receive training and resources to succeed. My background helps me understand what works and how to introduce it into the classroom. I am committed to raising academic standards and school ratings across the district. That means supporting strong instruction, clear accountability, and continuous improvement—while ensuring teachers have what they need to do their best work. I will listen to parents, teachers, and community members, work hard, and stay focused on the students and families who count on our schools. It would be an honor to earn your trust and your vote. paragraphs: I am a dedicated Union City mom, Chair of our City’s Human Relations Commission, and a cybersecurity program manager at a Fortune 500 company. My family moved to Union City in 2012 because we believed in our schools and community. Both of our daughters attended James Logan High School. One is now studying at UC Berkeley, and the other is a current Logan senior. When I vote on school district decisions, I will be voting for my own family, my neighbors, and every student in our community. Strong schools benefit everyone. They prepare our students for success, strengthen our neighborhoods, protect property values, and ensure taxpayer dollars are spent wisely. I taught engineering students in India and served three years as a substitute teacher in Bay Area classrooms. As a program manager I oversee multimillion-dollar budgets and bring results with transparency and accountability every day, and I will do the same on the school board. As your trustee, I will always put our students and community first. I am committed to being a leader for our district who shows up, listens, takes action, and delivers. I hope to earn your vote and together, let’s build a stronger New Haven Unified School District for all of us.

As a lifelong Union City resident, parent, and educator, I am committed to ensuring every learner in New Haven Unified School District has the opportunity to thrive in safe, welcoming, innovative, and excellent schools. For over 25 years, I served students, families, and schools as a teacher, principal, and leadership consultant. My experience includes Founding Principal of Emerald High School in Dublin Unified School District, the newest high school in Alameda County in 50 years, Principal of Milpitas High School, Silicon Valley’s largest high schools with 3,300 students, and teacher, activities director and administrator at James Logan High School, where I served our community for 16 years. Doctor of Education from UC Berkeley, my research focused on equitable opportunities for diverse students through culturally-responsive school leadership and community partnerships. Throughout my career, I have led school improvement efforts, managed multimillion-dollar budgets and construction projects, expanded STEAM, college and career readiness opportunities, and built partnerships with families, businesses, and the community. Schools are strongest when we prioritize academic excellence, student well-being, and meaningful collaboration with administrators, teachers, staff, and families. I will bring experience and collaborative leadership to the Board, always putting students first and preparing every learner for success in college, career, and life. Endorsed by New Haven Teachers Association and many East Bay leaders - I am honored to earn your vote.

paragraphs: As an attorney, and most importantly as a concerned parent, I am running to put our children, teachers, and classrooms first. Having attended nearly every board meeting last year, I consistently advocated for financial accountability and opposed teaching and student facing staff layoffs. PUSD’s recent fiscal challenges, including negative certification and depleted reserves, highlight the urgent need for sound, independent governance. Our dedicated teachers and support staff are the heart of our schools. I will bring independent oversight, rigorous analysis, and legal expertise to restore fiscal stability, rebuild budget reserves, and bring true transparency to district leadership. Protecting classroom resources and supporting our teaching staff will always be my top priority. Together, we can ensure PUSD remains a place where every child receives an extraordinary education and grows toward a bright future.

I’m excited about the future of the Pleasanton Unified School District, and I’m dedicated to supporting students, parents, teachers and schools. I will work with our Superintendent, Educators, and fellow Trustees to prioritize transparency, respect, and accountability in setting our district’s priorities. Over the last 18 years, I’ve been proud to have my four children attend Vintage Hills Elementary School, Pleasanton Middle School and Amador Valley High School. I look forward to representing these schools, Hearst Elementary School, and all of PUSD to maintain their excellence. I’ve volunteered at all grade levels and worked as a student teacher at PMS while getting my teaching credential. As a current engineering and robotics teacher at Livermore High School, I have experience with both the joys and the challenges of education. I also have 10 years of experience working as an aerospace engineer with a BA in Physics and an MS in Aerospace Engineering. I look forward to applying my experience as an educator, engineer and longtime Pleasanton resident to ensure the continued growth and both the short- and long-term financial health of our district. As a Pleasanton School Board Trustee, I will support student success while maintaining our high standards for academics.

contests.title: Sunol Glen Unified School District Governing Board Member

paragraphs: I am honored to be a candidate for the Sunol Glen School Board because I care deeply about our students, school, and community. My two daughters attended Sunol Glen School for three years, and although they have since moved on, our family remains actively involved in Sunol through the Sunol Girl Scout troop and the Sunol 4-H program. Professionally, I lead global cybersecurity compliance and physical security programs for Quanta Computer in Fremont. My work includes collaborating with executive leadership, managing complex programs, developing policies, and ensuring accountability across global operations. These experiences have strengthened my leadership, strategic planning, and decision-making skills, which I believe will benefit our school district. If elected, I will focus on supporting academic excellence, student safety, fiscal responsibility, and open communication between families, educators, and the community. I believe every student deserves a safe, inclusive, and inspiring learning environment where they can succeed. It would be an honor to serve on the Sunol Glen School Board and help ensure our school continues to provide outstanding opportunities for every student. SGUSD-1

As a mother, grandmother, and longtime member of our community, I believe our children deserve a safe, respectful learning environment where they can focus on reading, writing, math, science, and preparing for a successful future. I am not a career politician. I am a parent who understands the responsibility of helping children grow into capable, kind, and responsible adults. Raising a family has taught me that common sense, accountability, and compassion matter. While no one is perfect, life experience has given me the wisdom to recognize both the challenges our children face and the importance of protecting their hearts, minds, and futures. If elected, I will listen to parents, teachers, students, and our community. I believe every child deserves the opportunity to learn in a positive environment where they feel safe, respected, and encouraged to reach their full potential. I am running because I care deeply about the next generation. My goal is simple: to put students first, support academic excellence, practice fiscal responsibility, and help ensure our schools remain places where children can learn, grow, and thrive.

Sunol Glen School brought our family to Sunol 27 years ago. Drawn to this small town and small, high-performing school where everyone knows your name and helps your child thrive, our daughters attended K–8, receiving an exceptional education. Education has always been my family’s core value—my parents were a college professor and middle school teacher. I believe K–8 is the foundation for every child’s future. As Sunol Glen looks toward its next 100 years, I am running for Sunol Glen School Board to protect its legacy honoring generations of educators and Sunolians, preserve its uniqueness, and strengthen what keeps it exceptional and independent. I respectfully ask for your vote. I bring 34 years of business and technology experience at a Fortune 10 company, developing governance processes focusing limited resources on top priorities, turning plans into results by shaping strategy, building portfolios, benchmarking projects. This discipline, and my MBA and MS in Computer Science, directly support school board responsibilities. Degrees in Earthquake Seismology, Marine Geophysics, and Geology further prepare me for facilities and safety oversight. I serve as Treasurer of the Kilkare Woods Association, growing reserves and building multi-year asset plans. I’ve become a trusted advocate for a disabled friend’s business affairs.

statement.designation: Retired Dean of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics
paragraphs: As a Sunolian for over 20 years, I respectfully ask for your support to serve our community as a member of the Sunol Glen School Board. I am a product of California’s public education system. I attended public schools through high school before returning to college as an adult. I earned a Bachelor’s in Applied Mathematics from California State University, Bakersfield, and a Master’s in Statistics from the University of California, Santa Barbara. I devoted my career to public education, retiring in December 2025 after 25 years with California Community Colleges. I began as a Professor of Mathematics and Statistics 4 and most recently served as Dean of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics at Contra Costa College. In that role, I led faculty and staff, managed budgets, and oversaw hiring and evaluation processes. I also helped guide the successful completion of a $72 million Science Center bond project. I am a mother, grandmother and aunt who has supported children through Sunol Glen, and I’m committed to ensuring every Sunol Glen student receives a high-quality education in a safe, supportive, and fiscally responsible environment. I would be honored to bring my experience and skills to serve our students, school, and community.

paragraphs: Experience: I have served as Alameda Vice Mayor three times during my 22 years on City Council. I have a Master’s in City Planning from UC Berkeley, where I also earned my Bachelor’s degree: I am a full-time professional public sector urban planner. A life -long Filipino-American West Ender, I graduated from Encinal High School, where I was also Student Body President. My Mayoral Theme: “Making City Hall Responsive to Our Changing City and Needs.” Priority 1: I will end the police hiring freeze enacted by City Council. We have the revenues to hire the number of officers we’ve always targeted - i.e. 88 positions. There is no need to keep the Chief from filling the 88 positions. The “beach takeovers” and on -going traffic concerns demonstrate this freeze is ill-conceived. Priority 2: I will keep City Hall a welcoming place for all . . . building on my work for Alameda’s LGBTQ community (https://daysog.my.canva.site/equality), for transgender youths (https://alamedapost.com/news/city-council-endorses-new-lgbtq-action-plan/), and for faith communities under pressure (https://jweekly.com/2024/01/03/ cease-fire -letter-falls-flat-in-alameda-after-a-tense-5-hour-meeting/). Priority 3: I will create a new “infrastructure and sea level rise commission” to oversee key infrastructure (i.e. streets, sidewalks, sewerage), and to oversee shoreline sea level rise strategies. I humbly ask for your vote:

statement.designation: Alameda City Councilmember, Former Senior Services Administrator, Nonprofit Youth Services Board Member
paragraphs: I’m running to be Mayor of Alameda because our city needs responsible, proven leadership and my record of accomplishments has made life better for Alameda children, youth, families, and seniors. On the Alameda School Board I ensured that Bayport developers – not taxpayers, built Ruby Bridges Elementary School, and I led AUSD to be the first district in the country to reduce bullying by teaching children to respect all families. As Director of the Alameda Healthcare District, I kept Alameda Hospital open by holding Alameda Health System accountable for state seismic improvements. In 3.5 years as your Councilmember, I’ve improved pedestrian safety, expanded low-income housing, eliminated investments in weapons and polluters, and welcomed green tech and biotech economic engines to Alameda. I am endorsed by countless Alameda community members, including the state, county, and local elected officials who call Alameda home: Alameda County Supervisor Lena Tam, 4-term District Attorney Nancy O’Malley, and former State Senator Don Perata. I grew up in Alameda, and I left my job in Washington to raise my son with Alameda values: inclusivity, transparency, and responsiveness. My priorities are Alameda priorities: as your mayor I’ll focus on responsible development, living-wage jobs, emergency preparedness and environmental resiliency.

Serving you on the City Council for 8 years was an honor. I was results-oriented, accessible, and proactive in engaging with the community. Now I’m running to be your Mayor and promise to continue serving you the same way. An education executive, I have the professional experience to lead innovation and change – and as a native Alamedan with deep roots here, I’m committed to preserving what’s best about Alameda while moving us toward a vibrant future. We face so many threats to our quality of life – affordability, climate change, and more. I’m a businesswoman, educator, community volunteer, wife, and mother who understands those daily challenges. Let’s move Alameda forward together, delivering a better quality of life for all, championing transparency and accountability in public decision-making, and protecting vital city services and amenities. I’ll put my experience to work for you to expand housing affordability for all, keep neighborhoods distinct, improve pedestrian and bike safety, protect our shoreline, improve Alameda’s natural disaster preparedness, maintain police and fire response times, and prioritize economic development. Please join our Mayor Marilyn Ezzy Ashcraft, Councilmembers Michelle Pryor and Greg Boller, working families, and local leaders in support of my candidacy. I would be honored to have your vote. www.maliavella.com AMAY-1

statement.designation: Software Product Manager, Alameda Free Library Board President, Love Elementary School Site Council Secretary, Father
paragraphs: My career is focused on understanding hard problems and solving them. At the U.S. Digital Service, an arm of The White House during the Biden administration, I worked on modernizing the IRS to be faster and easier to use. I led product teams at Google. I built an Emmy-winning education app used by millions of students, which Google acquired. I’m doing that same work here, as President of the Alameda Free Library Board and on Love Elementary’s School Site Council, where the accountability is a lot closer to home. I’ve also walked every street of this Island with my daughters. Along the way I talked with hundreds of Alamedans. What I heard was pride. People love this Island, and they know what could make it better. A universal call for safer, slower streets. Longtime residents who want to stay but are worried about getting priced out. Vacant storefronts draining the life from our downtowns. Climate change hitting our infrastructure, like the lagoons in Bay Farm. These are solvable. I’m running to solve them, and I’d love to earn your vote to do that work. thushanforalameda.com ALCC-1

Dear Fellow Alamedans, my name is Maria Luisa Bondonno, and I seek your vote to serve as a Councilmember for the City of Alameda. My academic preparation includes a Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from San Francisco State University, a Master’s Degree in Communications from Cornell University, and a Juris Doctor from Hastings College of the Law. I began my career in public service as a Deputy Legislative Counsel for the State of California. I provided legal counsel to legislators, drafted approximately 100 bills per session, conducted legal research, prepared analytical memoranda, and testified before Legislative Committees—always advancing the public interest. In 2001, I joined the California Public Utilities Commission. I advised Supervisors, the General Counsel, and Commissioners on legal strategies affecting ratepayers. I attended closed sessions, presented oral arguments, developed litigation strategies for rehearing and appellate cases, authored Commission decisions, and represented the CPUC in appellate court. Throughout my career as a civil servant, my work has centered on rigorous legal analysis and the faithful protection of the public interest. I look forward to representing your interests to the best of my ability. I appreciate your support and your vote. Ademas, hablo espanol.

I love Alameda. We have the capacity and opportunity to care for our residents, businesses, nonprofits, neighbors, visitors and community in a manner that is unique and special because of the size of our city and the amount of people that contribute toward making Alameda a great place to live. I am an active community member, social work professional and mom to three Alameda Unified School District graduates. I am committed to youth, strengthening social services to support individuals and families in times of need and actively contributing to decisions that prioritize infrastructure improvements. As the former social services manager for the City of Alameda, I led youth and community groups like Alameda Collaboration for Children, Youth and their Families and worked across city departments to enhance social services and successfully deliver on projects that leveraged federal, state, county and city funding like Dignity Village and Queer Teen Alameda Center. I have extensive community engagement experience and most recently served as the executive director for Friends of the Alameda Free Library, where I remain an active volunteer. I know how the city works and I am a good listener. Vote for me and we can make Alameda a better community for all.

statement.designation: Technology Partner Manager, Little League Coach, Father
paragraphs: Alameda is the place I proudly call home and I believe we have an opportunity to thoughtfully plan for its future. It will take all of us working together to find creative solutions and move forward on the priorities that matter most. I have a background in energy and environmental policy, and after graduate school joined a clean tech startup advocating for increased sustainability. Since moving to Alameda, I’ve coached Alameda Little League and Alameda Youth Basketball and volunteered with local nonprofits supporting families and 4 neighbors. I recently served four years on the Alameda County Mosquito Abatement District Board, helping promote public health and environmental protection. As a Coro Fellow in Public Affairs, I learned the importance of working with everyone in our community to develop effective, lasting solutions. That’s why Alameda is better together. Our greatest strength has always been the people who show up, support one another, and bring their unique experiences and perspectives. Together, we can create safe, accessible streets, support thriving business districts, and make thoughtful investments in the infrastructure that will serve Alameda for decades to come. I’m excited for the opportunity to work alongside each of you to help build Alameda’s future.

I was born and raised in Alameda and graduated from Alameda High. Our kids graduated from Alameda High and our granddaughter is attending Alameda High. I am a member of the Board of Directors on the Alameda Citizens Taskforce. I will continue to preserve Alameda’s historic single family neighborhoods. I will continue to support the building of affordable housing in Alameda’s redevelopment areas. I will continue to support the excellence in our school system. My wife worked for the School District and our son is a teacher in the School District. I will continue helping build the upgrades to the school buildings. My company. Triple S Electric Co., wired up the Paden School remodel, the Washington School Remodel, the Height School remodel, the multipurpose buildings at Edison, Otis and Paden, and installed the underground at Ruby Bridges. I will continue to support the youth athletic programs like soccer and little league baseball. I will continue to work to complete the Veterans Center at the old Navy Base. I will continue to support our Police Department. I will support ending taxing of food eaten at restaurants. ALCC-2

I am running for City Council for good governance, for the environment, children and working families. I have worked as a community organizer and legislative leader on Barbara Boxer’s Senate and Barbara Lee’s State Senate campaigns, and coordinated the Kids First! Campaign, a $5.5 million youth fund. I co-founded Carnegie Library Innovation Hall Community Advisory Board and served on Rhythmix Cultural Works board. Fighting to protect our environment, I want to center city’s resources on the existential threat of climate change and sea level rise to protect our quality of life and ensure public safety. I led the effort to have City Council pass our Climate Emergency Declaration; founded 100K Trees for Humanity to plant over 400 trees for climate in our parks; and will support directing funds from the infrastructure bond to support our existing Climate Action and Shoreline Adaptation Plans. I supported our schools PTAs; served on AUSD Black Achievers Alliance, and Encinal HS Athletic Boosters. I will work for a more democratic and resilient community. I will work hard for our city as your City Council representative and continue to listen to, respect, and fight for your voice to be heard.
