paragraphs: Albany welcomed my son and me and gave us a home. As Sammy grew from a kindergartner into a UC Davis student, I became deeply involved in serving the community that embraced us. I’m president of the Albany Community Foundation, serve on the Albany Y board, spent nearly ten years on the Albany Education Foundation board, and founded Albany’s Pride. Running my small business for nearly twenty years has taught me to set priorities, make every dollar count, and answer for the results. I’m running on one promise: a relentless focus on Albany. That means safer streets, citywide traffic calming and sidewalks seniors can trust; a transparent City budget, with a clear public plan to replace approximately $1.1 million in annual revenue tied to Golden Gate Fields as it moves toward becoming a waterfront park; Solano and San Pablo Avenues where local businesses can open, stay, and thrive; and room for the families, teachers, and seniors who make Albany work. I’m proud to be endorsed by Mayor Peggy McQuaid and Vice Mayor Jennifer Hansen-Romero. I’ll listen first, decide in the open, and report back. I’d be honored to earn your vote and your #1 ranking. jondestin.com ACC-1

I grew up in Albany, graduated from UC Berkeley with a BA in American History, and then studied film theory and practice at SFSU. I lived and worked in the Berkeley Students Co-ops and remain a proponent of self-governing cooperatives. I believe government should express a generosity of spirit and strive to be open and anti-authoritarian. I believe inclusivity is founded on pluralism, freedom of choice, and separation of church and state. I am the founder of Context By Signal (contextbysignal.com), a web service offering wireless network analysis from an environmental perspective. My interests include ensuring that the voices of home owners and tenants can be heard, whether by increased opportunities for discussion or meaningful processes for feedback and complaint. I would like to talk about housing speculation and how we can minimize the price of housing for future generations. Local codes should be updated for the digital era including standards for privacy and encroachment. We should talk about the impact of wireless tech on the residential “noise floor” and how tech coexists with older homes using traditional infrastructure. Local government matters nationally. I’d like to ensure the block coordinator program is democratic and has appropriate oversight.

I have proudly served Albany as a former Mayor, Vice Mayor and current councilmember addressing collective goals around equity, opportunity, and empowerment. I made right on my promise when elected as the 1st ever Latino, to bring in a new era of leadership that would move Albany forward intentionally and responsibly. I have a proven track record of empowering Albany to actualize its potential, having delivered results while Mayor, that include but aren’t limited to achieving a balanced budget, divesting from fossil fuels, and supporting the revival of Dinner With Albany for our community. I am committed to Albany’s future, sensible housing, enhanced access to basic needs, advancing initiatives for equitable and accessible infrastructure, and supporting evidence-based policy that is culturally and socially relevant. As a father to young children in Albany, the future of our city is personal. I am proud to be endorsed by Albany City Councilmembers and past Mayors John Miki & Preston Jordan, Albany School Board President Josh Mahoney, Albany School Board Trustees Sadia Khan & Becky Hopwood, State Senator Jesse Arregufn, Berkeley Mayor Adena Ishii, Contra Costa County Supervisor John Gioia and many others. Visit Albanyforward.org. Friends, rank Robin López #1 on your ballot!

For the past 27 years, I have proudly called Albany home, serving as a resident, volunteer, coach, parent, and public servant. As my son grew up here, I supported our schools through fundraising and student programs and spent many years coaching Little League baseball, where I became known as “Coach Chris.” Coaching allowed me to mentor young people and teach teamwork, accountability, and respect. Professionally, I bring more than 30 years of public service with the City and County of San Francisco, serving in Emergency Management, the Department of Public Works, and the Public Utilities Commission, where I have been entrusted with managing operations, budgets, and capital programs totaling billions of dollars. My career has given me extensive experience in government operations, infrastructure, emergency preparedness, strategic planning, budgeting, and delivering quality public services. This combination of community involvement and professional experience has prepared me to serve Albany effectively. I am committed to responsible stewardship of public resources, organizational efficiency, and thoughtful long-term planning. Above all, I lead with integrity and collaboration, listening, building partnerships, and helping ensure Albany remains an exceptional place to live, work, and raise a family. ACC-2 high-

Albany has always been my home; I feel lucky to have grown up here and I want to do everything I can to make it a better place and give back to my community. That is why I ran for Council in 2020, why I served as Councilmember, Vice-Mayor, and Mayor between 2020 & 2024, and why I have continued to give back since leaving the Council. In my time on Council I was proud to secure $600,000 in annual funding from UC Berkeley for our Fire Department and city services, keeping our budget intact when Golden Gate Fields closed. I believe our 4 City should be guided by smart, progressive policymaking, and I know that I can help lead with the values that our community shares. Professionally, I work for the Alameda County Housing and Community Development Department creating affordable housing. I serve as the Chair of the City’s Housing Advisory Commission and the President of the School District’s Citizen Bond Oversight Committee. I am proud to be endorsed by Albany City Councilmembers and past Mayors John Miki & Preston Jordan, Albany School Board President Josh Mahoney, and Albany School Board Trustees Sadia Khan & Becky Hopwood, State Senator Jesse Arreguin, Berkeley Mayor Adena Ishii, Former State Senator Nancy Skinner and many others. paragraphs: I love Albany and believe our public schools are the heart of our community. My two children attend Ocean View Elementary and Albany Children’s Center. I work as a Vice President of Finance for a healthcare organization, where I provide financial oversight and strategic direction on multi-year plans. I am eager to bring that expertise to benefit Albany schools. For the past two years, I have served on the Citizens’ Bond Oversight Committee, which tracks how our district spends bond funds, and the Ocean View School Site Council, ensuring the school programs are meeting students’ needs. Excellent schools need fantastic teachers who feel supported. If elected, I promise to listen to and engage with our teachers, staff, and parents, carrying their values into every board decision. All six campuses deserve strong academic performance, safe buildings, and reliable support for every student. I will closely examine the district budget and master plan and push for long-term fiscal stability and educational equity. I bring executive financial oversight, deep appreciation for our educators, and a parent’s perspective to the board. I would be honored to earn your vote this November.

I have served on the Albany School Board for five years – first from 2020 to 2024 and now since 2025 to fill an unexpected vacancy. My family and I have lived in Albany for 13 years. Our two daughters will attend Albany High this year and have spent their entire school careers in Albany. I love our community and our schools. Getting a good education changed my life, and I moved here to give my children access to our exceptional schools and teachers. Public education is the great equalizer in our society. When it reaches its full potential, it gives our children the opportunity to reach theirs, regardless of how much money they have, where they are from, how they learn, or any other aspect of their identity or background. I approach this position with respect and without ego. I’ve learned a great deal from my previous years on the Board. As an attorney and professional coach, I know how to make difficult decisions in a calm, level-headed way. And I am passionate about achieving equity. I would be grateful for the chance to continue putting my skills and experience to work in service of our students and their families.

For 24 years, Albany has been my home. It’s where I raised my three children, who attended Albany schools from kindergarten through 12th grade before going on to college. I have volunteered extensively in our schools and community and, as a member of the Board of Education, helped lead successful parcel tax and bond measure campaigns to provide critical funding for Albany students. I’ve served as Board president and vice president and worked to support equity, academic excellence, student well-being, fiscal responsibility, and strong partnerships with families and staff. A former registered nurse and midwife, I bring a calm, thoughtful, and detail-oriented approach to problem-solving and public service. Our district has experienced significant change in recent years, including the loss of our superintendent, new district administrators, and Board turnover. During times of transition, experienced leadership matters. I bring the stability, continuity, and steady governance needed to support our students, staff, and families while helping AUSD continue to thrive. I’m endorsed by School Board Vice President Inkeles; former Board Presidents Hinkley, Trutane, and Rosenbaum; Albany City Council Members López, Miki, and Jordan; and former Mayors Tiedemann and Pilch. I would be honored to earn your vote for re-election to the Board. ABE-1

I’m seeking re-election to the Albany School Board. During my two years on the Board, including time as Board President, I’ve been part of the Committee to pass Measure L, which has raised $64M in bonds to help with school facilities. I’ve helped steer the Facilities Master Plan to develop an infrastructure plan for the next 25+ years. Most impactfully, during my tenure, we’ve seen meaningful District focus and student progress in reading, in particular, for our most vulnerable and historically marginalized students. As we look forward, my focus is in three areas. First, in these uncertain economic times, we must 4 remain financially stable, so that Albany can decide how to best educate Albany kids. Second, our kids must have safe facilities and an environment conducive to learning. Finally, most importantly, we must address the issues of equity -- ensuring that all students can achieve the required standards for reading and math, so as to have the foundation to follow their passions and pursue the path they desire. I’m a parent of two recent graduates from Albany High. My kids were able to find their communities and thrive in our schools. I want that opportunity for all kids in Albany.

I believe that a high-quality public education provides learning environments where students feel safe within a supportive community; where students can find and pursue their passions; and where students are equipped with the resources and support they need to succeed in school and beyond. I have been working in education for 21 years. After receiving my Masters in Teaching from Columbia University Teachers College, I taught middle school science for eight years and math for four of those eight years. I left the classroom to pursue a PhD in Education, which I received from Johns Hopkins University School of Education. I am now an education researcher with expertise in student motivation and STEM education. I am also a parent of a student at Cornell Elementary, where I serve on the School Site Council. Together, this enables me to look at what is happening within our schools from the lens of a researcher, a teacher, and a parent. As a member of the AUSD Board of Education I will work collaboratively to enact policies and spending that foster exceptional educational environments that provide students with the best opportunity to grow into thriving members of our community.

contests.title: Rent Stabilization Board Commissioners, Berkeley

paragraphs: I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am a Berkeley tenant, a Tenant Organizer with the Alliance of Californians for Community Empowerment, the Chair of the Berkeley Tenants Union, and head of the Berkeley Tenant Organizing Task Force. As a formerly homeless tenant who has faced landlord negligence, I have firsthand experience using the resources of the Rent Stabilization Board to advocate for my rights. I organized Berkeley Tenants Union, Local #2 in my own building, one of the largest unionized buildings in Berkeley. I utilized the power of that union to resolve health and safety problems – including a severe cockroach infestation and heating issues – while negotiating rent reductions for tenants. Through my work helping hundreds of tenants form unions under the Berkeley Tenant Protection and Right to Organize Act, I have routinely encountered housing conditions unfit for life. From medical issues like asthma resulting from black mold in apartments, to mobility-impaired seniors forced to scale multiple flights of stairs during frequent elevator outages, tenants face uninhabitable conditions while paying exorbitant rents. I am running to hold slumlords accountable, and to make housing more affordable for Berkeley. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

As the appointee of Mayor Jesse Arreguin (now California State Senator Arreguin) to the Homeless Services Panel of Experts which I chair) I have been endorsed by Senator Arreguin for Berkeley Rent Board. My extensive policy experience and service in the City of Berkeley provides me with the skills and local government knowledge to serve as a Rent Board commissioner. As a strong supporter of rent control, critical in these times of increasingly unaffordable rents, I plan to focus my work on anti-displacement, disability, and anti-discrimination issues. My extensive experience in these areas includes developing commission recommendations I have written and presented to Council. The Rent Board must be client-friendly to both tenants and small landlords, making the necessary services, education and outreach available as to laws, regulations, rights and responsibilities, operating efficiently honoring the intent of the Rent Stabilization Ordinance in a fiscally responsible manner. As a 24 year Berkeley tenant with over 17 years of experience on citizens’ advisory commissions, I have regularly made both policy and budgetary recommendations to Council, exercising oversight over programs, addressing housing and homelessness policy, equity, planning and accountability. As an analytical, community-based critical thinker, I developed balanced positions in a collaborative manner.

I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am an incumbent Rent Board Commissioner running for reelection to continue my work of making housing more climate resilient, my main goal as Chair of the Rent Board Climate Resilience and Habitability Committee. Tenants are particularly vulnerable to temperature fluctuations and increasingly unhealthy air quality because they are unable to make structural changes to their homes. I support expanding homeowner-focused initiatives for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and weatherization to include all housing. I have been fighting for protecting and expanding rent control, because I am aware of the dire homelessness trajectory for the elderly, the ravages of gentrification, and general unaffordability of living in Berkeley. Rent control plays a pivotal role in enabling tenants to remain in place and age with dignity, without being constructively evicted through lack of maintenance, unsafe conditions, or intimidation. I studied International Relations and Environmental Law. As an employee with the California Department of Justice, I have dedicated my career to civil service, and am a shop steward with SEIU Local 1000. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am an incumbent Rent Board Commissioner running to continue enforcing justice for tenants facing unfair eviction and unstable housing. A graduate from UC Berkeley’s Legal Studies Program and more recently a law student at UC Law San Francisco, I recently worked as a Law Clerk for Centro Legal de la Raza, where I fought to keep tenants safe in their homes. I am passionate about equity for all Berkeley residents. I fought for the passage of Berkeley Measure BB, the Berkeley Tenant Protection and Right to Organize Act, which expanded tenant protections and enshrined a tenant right to organize. I served as the Vice-Chair of the Berkeley Police Accountability Board, where I focused on fostering community trust through police oversight. I also served as Chair of Berkeley’s Reimagining Public Safety Task Force. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will continue to fight for equity and justice in Berkeley, prioritizing greater community awareness of tenant rights and stronger legal protections from housing discrimination, substandard living conditions, and illegal evictions. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

statement.designation: Attorney / Meditation Teacher / 94.1 KPFA Radio Host Producer and Programmer
paragraphs: I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. Having served as a Public Defender in Santa Clara County and an attorney at the Eviction Defense Center, I know that stable, affordable and habitable housing is the foundation of a healthy community. I believe that we must treat housing as a necessity, not a tool for financial exploitation. Since 2013, I have been a host/producer on KPFA analyzing complex current events from a mulitracial and feminist perspective. I am also a Meditation Teacher. I have raised two sons in a rent-controlled apartment in Berkeley since 2006. I am running to keep rent-controlled apartments habitable and expand affordability options for all Berkeley residents. I will protect tenants, preserve existing affordable housing, and fund new affordable homes – especially for seniors, people with disabilities, essential workers, and students. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will work towards a future where everyone can enjoy safe, habitable, accessible, and energy efficient housing. I will fight to keep our city economically and ethnically diverse and one which works for all. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am a UC Berkeley student, Army veteran, tenant organizer, and public servant. I have spent the last seven years in service to my country, and my community. Born in the Bay Area and emancipated at 17, I served active duty in the U.S. Army, and now serve part time in the California Army National Guard. I carried that commitment to public service into local government, where I helped residents navigate housing issues, social services, and county programs at the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors. I have served as Field Director for local and statewide campaigns, personally knocked thousands of doors, organized with unionizing workers, and built grassroots power through the Berkeley Tenant Organizing Task Force. I organized my building, forming The Bishop Tenants Association, and currently run workshops to educate tenants about their rights. I am running because every tenant deserves safe, stable, and dignified housing. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will expand tenant organizing power, fight wrongful evictions, and ensure rent protections work in practice – not just on paper — for students, workers, and families. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

contests.title: School Directors, Berkeley

paragraphs: As a proud Berkeley Unified graduate, educator, parent, and current School Board President, it has been an honor to serve our community. As the youngest School Board President and first active classroom teacher elected to the Board, I have brought a vital perspective to every decision, ensuring that the voices of students, families, and educators remain at the center of our work. As a district we’ve guided our schools through unprecedented challenges while laying the foundation for the future. Together, we’ve navigated difficult fiscal realities, strengthened student mental health supports, modernized district systems, and advanced policies to create safer and more inclusive schools. I know firsthand that a high-quality public education can transform lives. Students deserve rigorous academics, safe and welcoming schools, and the support necessary to reach their fullest potential. If re-elected, I will continue working to close opportunity gaps, strengthen academic achievement, expand college and career pathways, invest in student well-being, promote high quality teaching, and ensure responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars. I am proud to have earned the support of educators, parents, students, and community leaders, and I respectfully ask for your vote to continue building a stronger Berkeley Unified for every student.

I am Sandy Park—a 25-year public education veteran, current BUSD parent of three, active community organizer, and first-generation daughter of immigrants. Endorsed by the Berkeley Federation of Teachers, my career spans classroom teaching, athletic coaching, central administration, and strategic consulting with California school districts. I am committed to equitable fiscal stewardship, protecting student-facing services, and supporting our educators and classified staff. My platform centers on pro-active governance: establishing forward-thinking AI and technology policies that safeguard student privacy while embracing digital innovation, closing the opportunity gap, and fostering a culture of shared decision-making. True equity requires targeted, structural investments so students furthest from baseline standards receive the resources needed to thrive — without taking away from any child. By building trust and transparency with our community, the Board can focus on long-term collaborative solutions that move our district forward.

I am a current BUSD Board Director, U.C. Berkeley Ph.D., community college chemistry teacher, and parent of two BUSD kids. I currently serve on the BUSD Career and Technical Education Advisory Committee, BUSD Facilities Committee, BUSD Bond Oversight Committee, Districtwide Parent Teacher Council, and Superintendent’s Budget Advisory Committee. I have co-chaired two committees for funding Berkeley’s schools, passed in 2022 and 2024, that provide funding for competitive teacher salaries, improved facilities and maintenance, small class sizes, libraries, and music programs. On the school board, I have championed safe student drop-offs, aftercare expansion, gender neutral bathrooms, BHS tennis courts, and co-authored two student-sponsored resolutions focused on climate resiliency. I am not a career politician; I am a teacher, parent, and labor organizer committed to the future of public education for all kids. I continue to be committed to closing BUSD’s persistent achievement gaps, expanding STEAM (science, technology, engineering, art, and mathematics) opportunities for all students, improving recruitment and retention of teachers and staff, supporting approved improvements to curriculum (including math and literacy), and authentically engaging with our community. Please visit shanoski4berkeley.nationbuilder.com for a complete list of endorsements.

contests.title: Member Of City Council District #1, Berkeley

paragraphs: Proudly endorsed by the Berkeley Fire Fighters Association, Local 1227. Berkeley City Council needs leaders with a proven record of governing effectively, managing public dollars responsibly, and delivering results for the people they serve. With an estimated $30M deficit, our neighborhood cannot afford another politician more focused on satisfying lobbyists than serving our community. We need a leader who listens, understands government, and turns priorities into results. That is why I am running. I learned during my 10 years as an education advocate that no one will fight for your kids like you will. So, I stepped up. As an elected official, I made fiscal oversight and accountability a priority while increasing pay, saving jobs, prioritizing student outcomes, advancing climate sustainability, and building educator housing. I’m ready to bring that same governing experience to District One. As a Financial Controller managing global budgets, I know fiscal management is essential. Our tax dollars must protect our first responders, build truly affordable housing, keep our streets paved, address homelessness with lasting solutions, and help small businesses thrive. My family has called District One home for generations. I know its strengths, experience its challenges, and will fight for those who live here today. Proudly endorsed by State Senator Jesse Arreguin. Vote Laura Babitt! www.laura4d1.com Listen. Connect. Deliver.

I’m running for City Council to build an affordable, safe, green, and thriving Berkeley for everyone. I’ve spent the past 15 years working on environmental efforts around the world, and now I’m excited to focus my efforts on my local community. As a new father, I’m committed to keeping our community safe and welcoming, making it easier to get around for people of all abilities, and working to ensure we create more housing at all income levels so our kids can afford to live here when they grow up. As Councilmember, I’ll green our community by planting more trees, advocating for our parks, and fighting climate change with clean energy and sustainable transportation. I’ll support our first responders and local businesses, fix our streets and sidewalks, and work to tackle our housing and homelessness crises with citywide solutions and regional partners. I bring a pragmatic, progressive perspective to ensuring Berkeley delivers exceptional city services and spends tax dollars wisely. I will prioritize constituent services. I’m proud to be endorsed by the Berkeley Firefighters Association, the Sierra Club, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, along with additional elected and community leaders. I hope to earn your vote as well. Join us:

Repair Our Streets. Save Our Waterfront. Keep Flock Out. As your city council representative, I will forward an agenda of accountability, affordability, and community. Working at the California Public Utilities Commission, I am proud to hold a record of achievement on clean energy initiatives, utility regulation, and protecting everyday Californians from fraud. As someone who has revised billion-dollar budgets, I am not afraid to take on our ballooning deficit and balance our City’s budget. I will work with the city to maintain infrastructure, expand climate resilience, and provide dignified housing and services for the unhoused. Berkeley needs a community-centered vision. Working with community land trusts and non-profits, I will focus on building on our successes in affordable housing growth, while expanding community and open spaces. I will work to improve tenant protections and fight housing speculation that results in empty building shells and pushes out our local businesses. I will develop green spaces in West Berkeley and protect our waterfront. Berkeley can be a more affordable city — a sustainable city that supports its residents and improves the quality of life for all. As our city grows and changes, we must live by the guiding principle: We take care of us.

I’m Steve Kromer, and I’m running for City Council in District 1. I’ve had many addresses in Berkeley over the last 37 years, but good luck, and my dog Wilson, led me to the neighborhood I now call home. You can find us at James Kenney Park almost every morning. That’s my first reason for running: I love this park. I run the Friends of James Kenney Park email list and help organize our clean-up days, working alongside the neighbors and volunteers who look after the place we share. Parks are where a neighborhood becomes a community. Second, transparency. I’ve spent my career measuring whether public dollars deliver what they promise — as a Professional Engineer and a nonprofit treasurer. Our parks’ budgets, and the city’s, should be open and honest. You deserve to see where your money goes. Third, efficient city government. Berkeley doesn’t lack good ideas — it lacks follow-through. I know how to turn plans into results that hold up after the meeting ends. Running for office is how I give back. Democracy starts at home, in our neighborhoods and parks. My first promise as your representative is simple: I will listen. Really listen. Listen, listen, listen.

Berkeley faces two questions: how do we deliver effective, fiscally-responsible city services, and how do we uphold our progressive values and protect our most vulnerable neighbors? Too many politicians tell us we must choose. I don’t believe that. My name is Daria Wrubel, and I’m running to prove Berkeley can be both well run and true to its values. I’m a lifelong Berkeley resident, a former Berkeley public school garden teacher, a licensed marriage and family therapist, and a former union organizer. I’ve spent years helping our young people through a mental health system that too often fails them. As an organizer, I learned that real change comes from bringing people together, not driving them apart. I’m running to build housing and protect tenants, because those goals belong together. I’m running to invest in public safety that keeps us safe without mass-surveillance, and without risking further harm to immigrants, trans neighbors, and everyone the current federal administration has targeted. District 1 residents deserve experienced representation that delivers for them and their neighbors. Learn more about my campaign and how you can join us at https://www.dariaforberkeley.com/. I’d be honored to earn your vote.

statement.designation: Trust and Safety Policy, Small Business Owner
paragraphs: I am Majdi Gaith, an independent progressive, former Peace and Justice Commissioner, Trust and Safety policy professional, small business co-founder, parent, and UC Berkeley graduate running for Berkeley City Council, District 4. For more than a decade, I have developed policies that protect millions of people from harassment, fraud, abuse, and emerging threats. This work taught me how to evaluate evidence, solve complex problems, build consensus, and make balanced decisions that strengthen public trust. I am building a multicultural, multifaith, and multigenerational coalition because Berkeley is strongest when people from every background and generation work together. As the co-founder of a local coffee roasting business and bakery, I understand the challenges facing small businesses, workers, and our neighborhood commercial corridors. As a parent raising a family in Berkeley, I know every resident deserves safe streets, reliable city services, attainable housing, and the opportunity to thrive. I will bring thoughtful leadership, fiscal responsibility, transparency, and integrity to City Hall. I will work to revitalize downtown and our neighborhood commercial corridors, strengthen tenant protections, support workers and local businesses, expand housing opportunities, improve public safety, advance climate action, and ensure Berkeley’s government is accountable, responsive, and committed to protecting the rights, dignity, and opportunity of every resident.

When you elected me two years ago, I promised to be accessible, attentive, and focused on solving our city’s most pressing needs. Together we secured new housing at every income level, including affordable homes downtown; advanced street safety and accessibility improvements across our district; brought Downtown commercial vacancies down to pre-pandemic levels while investing in our small businesses and the arts; and reopened Civic Center Park as a public commons that everyone can enjoy. Still, we face challenges, including significant federal budget cuts and rising costs. I’m placing my decades of experience to work for you. We must continue to advance homeownership opportunities and rentals that hardworking residents can afford, help the unhoused find the supportive housing and wraparound services they deserve, and implement safer, climate-resilient infrastructure. I’m proud to be endorsed by the Sierra Club, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon, California Attorney General Rob Bonta, Mayor Adena Ishii, supermajorities of the City Council and Rent Board, every Berkeley School Boardmember, Supervisor Nikki Fortunato Bas, State Senators Jesse Arreguín and Aisha Wahab, Alameda County Sheriff Yesenia Sanchez our BART, AC Transit, East Bay Regional Parks, and East Bay Municipal Utility District directors, and 100+ neighbors and community leaders. We’re just getting started. I’d be honored to earn your vote for a full term so we can continue to make Berkeley a place we can all call home.

contests.title: Member Of City Council District #7, Berkeley

paragraphs: District 7 is my home. I live on Telegraph and have lived in Southside since 2016. I am a UC Berkeley graduate and clinical health worker who previously served as Vice Chair of Berkeley’s Homeless Commission. There, I moved and amended the People’s First Sanctuary Encampment recommendation, which centered clean water, sanitation, privacy, and resident decision-making. I have organized around People’s Park since 2017 and served meals through East Bay Food Not Bombs. I’m running because Southside needs a councilmember who can turn community needs into practical city action. I will protect rent-controlled housing and expand permanent affordability. I will prioritize sidewalk, lighting, sanitation, and disability-access improvements. I will work to make major development fund the infrastructure its growth demands and press UC Berkeley for housing and neighborhood responsibility. I will seek voter approval before major public land is converted and publish quarterly progress reports on housing stability, street repairs, public space, and local business conditions. Students, renters, workers, local business owners, and longtime neighbors deserve a councilmember they can reach and results they can see. I ask for your first-choice vote.

I was born, raised, and educated in Berkeley, graduating from UC Berkeley with degrees in Economics and Public Policy in December 2025. As an organizer and student advocate, I’m deeply committed to making Berkeley more affordable and accessible to students and marginalized community members. In 2024, I was elected as the Transfer Student Representative in the Associated Students of the University of California. I worked towards the creation of re-entry student housing and wrote grants for lighting across University Village. At Cal, I was a member of the “Black Triad” (African American Student Development, Black Student Union, and Black Recruitment and Retention Center), Cal Young Democratic Socialists of America, and the Berkeley Student Food Collective. During my last semester at Cal I served as a Campus Organizer with the Alameda Labor Council, leading the UC Berkeley “Get Out the Vote” campaign for Prop 50. I have worked with East Bay Alliance for a Sustainable Economy to organize Black workers and build labor power in my community. Currently, I serve on Berkeley’s Housing Advisory Commission for District 7. There, I have voted to hold landlords accountable, fund improved housing infrastructure, support affordable housing development, and renovate existing affordable housing. I strongly believe that housing is a human right, that living should be affordable, and that everyone should feel safe in our city. I am honored to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America, UAW Region 6, the Berkeley Tenants Union, Telegraph for People, and Alameda County Supervisor Nikki Fortunato Bas – learn more at syrakforsouthside.com.

contests.title: Member Of City Council District #8, Berkeley

paragraphs: It has been a privilege and a pleasure to serve as the District 8 Councilmember for these past four years, and I remain committed to putting essential public services and infrastructure first. In my first term, we’ve enhanced District 8 parks and replaced the Willard Clubhouse with a new, award-winning facility; supported our first responders with superb police and fire chiefs, new technology, and better wildfire preparedness; began investing in smoother, safer streets; updated our zoning laws to enable middle-density homes; and supported community events like the Elmwood Music Festival, Russell Street Halloween, Berkeley Sun Day, and more. There’s still much to be done, so I’m asking for your vote to continue working with you to improve public safety, support our small businesses, fix our streets and sidewalks, and make our city more inclusive and affordable. My pragmatic and collaborative approach is why my colleagues want to work with me for another 4 years. I’m proud to have the endorsements of State Senator Jesse Arreguín, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, Mayor of Berkeley Adena Ishii and a supermajority of the Berkeley City Council, Berkeley Firefighters Association Local 1227, the Sierra Club, Berkeley School Board Director Jennifer Shanoski, AC Transit Director Jean Walsh, BART Board Director Barnali Ghosh, Peralta Community College Trustee Dyana Delfin-Polk, and more. Join us:

I’m running for City Council District 8 bringing accountable leadership that listens to and respects the needs of Elmwood. I’ll fight hard to preserve it with growth that’s responsible and honors its legacy, which I understand because I’m part of it. I attended Willard Junior High and worked my first job at Colby Pharmacy, a small family business representing its core. I have over 15 years of experience navigating the difficulties of complex issues, including as an elected leader, a Unite Here 2850 union leader, Housing Commission vice-chair and organizer in the Friends of Adeline. Powerful lobbies are influencing leadership to up-zone and infill neighborhoods under the pretense of addressing our so-called housing crisis, including legislation benefitting investors with density bonuses. This doesn’t capture the affordable housing we need and is locally threatening the viability of our small businesses and neighborhood infrastructure, using oversimplified narratives that more is better. It’s not if it’s irresponsible and destructive. What’s required is mindful and responsible leadership who listens and ensures housing, safety, infrastructure, access and accessibility. We can’t afford politics as usual. People have the power. Let’s use ours to vote for accountable leadership and needed change. Vote Mari Nov 3.

Having grown up, raising kids, and caring for elderly family members here in Berkeley, I’ve watched our city change over decades. While shifts occur gradually, the cumulative stress on our community is clear. As an engineer, I analyze data to make sound policy decisions rather than serving special interests or selling out our city to large corporations. I am committed to clean, safe streets, supporting public education, and preserving our parks and open spaces for families across all generations. Living in a Zone Zero neighborhood, fire and earthquake safety are urgent priorities; I will foster close collaboration between the city, fire department, and residents so we can survive a major disaster together. Additionally, development must be balanced—protecting small businesses while accounting for traffic and infrastructure. In the university area, housing policy must protect our neighborhoods and student residents from exploitation while ensuring quality of life. Finally, we must proactively engage the University of California, Berkeley to ensure this large entity respects the integrity, value, and character of our city. Join our cause at wallmandistrict8.com.

contests.title: Auditor, Berkeley

paragraphs: During this last term, I have continued to take on some of Berkeley’s most pressing issues. Leveraging 26 years of auditing experience, I have produced impactful reports on leases, staff shortages and retention, restaurant inspections, homeless response, performance metrics, fire inspections spending, and contracts that did not go through competition. When the city faced a budget deficit, our office conducted an analysis about its financial condition that helped to inform budget discussions and decisions. Our audits have impacted City policy and contributed to additional funding for street paving. I’m proud that during my tenure, four of our audits have won national awards from the Association of Local Government Auditors. We also established a new whistleblower program for city employees to report fraud, waste and abuse of city resources. If reelected, I will complete audits of the public health division, the Rent Board, business license taxes and will identify other audits based on community needs. I will continue to conduct clear, objective and independent analysis and promote transparency in Berkeley government. I would be honored to have your support. Please visit www.jennyforauditor.com for a complete list of endorsements.

contests.title: Mayor, Dublin

paragraphs: Dublin needs a leader who listens, acts on residents’ concerns, and has proven experience and vision to guide our diverse city. It’s about preserving Dublin residents’ quality of life. My wife and I have lived in Dublin for 32 years. I’ve had a successful 40-year career managing the financial resources of large multinational corporations. In six years on the city council, I have served as Mayor and Vice Mayor, and served on boards and committees focusing on transportation, water resources, financial management, economic development, and housing. I will continue to put my experience and care for our city to work for you advocating for: Strong Public Safety. Mandate investments in safety programs and security infrastructure to ensure our residents remain safe. Economic Vitality. Support small businesses and attract new industries, broadening our business community and creating local jobs. Affordable Housing. As a critical part of our residential strategy, introduce creative solutions so essential workers, new families and seniors can afford to live in Dublin. Sustainable Environment. Reduce traffic congestion while preserving remaining open space and conserving natural resources. It will be my honor to represent you as Dublin’s Mayor. Learn more about my platform at

Dublin is a city built for possibility. As it continues to grow, I believe our responsibility is to ensure that growth improves the everyday lives of the people who call Dublin home. My work in human-centered systems design starts with a simple idea: systems work better when they are designed around the people who use them. I want to bring that approach to City Hall—listening to residents, identifying where our systems create unnecessary friction, and developing practical solutions around how people actually live. As Mayor, I will prioritize thoughtful growth, public safety, transportation and mobility, thriving local businesses, responsible use of public resources, and neighborhoods where people feel connected to their community. I believe residents deserve a city government that is accessible, transparent, responsive, and willing to rethink processes that no longer serve them well. Decisions should begin with understanding their real-world impact on residents. Dublin’s next chapter should not simply happen to us. We should design it together. I am running for Mayor to build a city that works better for everyone. I respectfully ask for your vote. DMAY-1

contests.title: Members Of City Council #2, Dublin

paragraphs: I am a passionate citizen and public servant who wants to represent you in District 2 on the Dublin City Council. I have 27 years of U.S. Army leadership experience where I led large organizations, served as an intelligence professional, and delivered results when it mattered most. I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Public Safety Administration, a Master’s of Public Administration, and a Master’s of Leadership Studies with emphasis in Community Engagement. paragraphs: I’m your neighbor, a regular working dog mom you’d see walking all over our beloved town and at community events like coastal cleanups. When ICE started terrorizing our cities after the 2024 election, I was afraid. Instead of running away, I decided to find ways a laid-off technical manager could use her skills to protect our sanctuary city. In 2023, our city council approved Flock cameras spying on us 24/7 in several high-density areas. ICE uses data Flock gathers about when we’re not home, where we commute, shop, and drop our kids off at school. All of us, not just criminals. Flock sells that data, stores it insecurely, and coaches local police to sell this grift to cities like ours. We need a councilwoman who asks the right questions and sees through big tech’s lies. We need an organized manager to keep important projects on track. Because more housing equals lower rents. Shorter delays keep roads safe and open. I believe we need to get big money out of politics, so I’m running a truly grassroots DIY campaign supported entirely by volunteers, free from annoying ads and drama. Let’s get things done instead. corry4emeryville.com ECC-1

I have lived in Emeryville for 18 years and am proud to raise my family here. I’ve served on Emeryville City Council since 2022 including as the Mayor of Emeryville last year. During my time on council, my focus has been on public safety and ensuring we have clean and well-maintained streets, sidewalks and public spaces. Beyond these core priorities, I have worked to make Emeryville more livable and sustainable. I expanded bike and pedestrian infrastructure, improved our parks, and introduced citywide environmental initiatives, including electrifying our municipal vehicle fleet. I support smart economic 4 growth through new housing and attracting businesses that strengthen our community and local economy. As Mayor, I stood up for our values by partnering with the Governor’s office, local elected officials and mayors to protect our community from ICE. Prior to serving on City Council, I gained experience on Emeryville’s Planning Commission and through my professional background as an engineer and project manager in the biotech industry. My public service is grounded in a love for this city and seeing our government work well for the people it serves. We’ve made a lot of progress as a city, but we still have a long way to go.

As a foster care kid from Brooklyn, I fought bullies. I did not back down, and neither should you. I remain the people’s councilmember, your public advocate. Whenever you felt unsafe, ignored, or pushed aside, you came to me. I listened, prayed or meditated, asked uncomfortable questions of those in power, and acted. The Obama White House named me a Champion of Change for my work as a tech innovator, entrepreneur, and educator. As a democratic socialist, I believe City Hall should put working people before corporate power. Since you elected me, I’ve made it harder for City Hall to ignore you, and my proposals are moving Emeryville towards fiscal accountability. I fight for renters, homeowners, mom-and-pop businesses, artists, and ethical governance that stops backroom deals. Life should mean thriving, not living paycheck to paycheck. Rent is too damn high. I pushed for a vacancy tax so empty buildings contribute to Emeryville’s future. I can be long-winded and theatrical, but I refuse to let City Hall hide what affects you. When there is no seat at the table, I bring my own chair. This seat is the people’s seat. The fight is in me. Fight with me.

I’ve called our community home for three-quarters of my life. From growing up on the North Oakland border to living in the Triangle Neighborhood and now Emery Bay Village, my roots run deep. My parents still live in my childhood home. They are active Emeryville Senior Center members who remind me of what makes our community so special. With a master’s in public policy from Georgetown University and over a decade of policy and communications experience serving federal agencies and private enterprise, I bring real technical expertise to local government. I know our street-level realities firsthand—from chaotic drop-offs at Anna Yates to gaps in our housing inventory, as well as public safety challenges in our neighborhoods and commercial hubs. I’m running to ensure fiscally sensible solutions to keep Emeryville safe, livable, and centered on the people who call it home. This means building walkable and bike-friendly streets that protect children and seniors, expanding housing access so anyone who wants to live in Emeryville can afford to stay, aligning stakeholders to take realistic, equitable steps toward improving public safety, and managing land use and development so that corporate interests don’t outweigh residents’ needs. I’d be honored to earn your vote. Visit brandonsoublet.com.

I will continue working with our community to increase access to parks and open space. I will expand on our progress to bring smart solutions to fix our roads and pedestrian infrastructure. I will implement individualized solutions for our unhoused neighbors, moving away from failed, one-size-fits-all programs. I will collaborate with the Police Department to increase staffing, protect property, and ensure every resident feels safe. I will work to streamline processes to attract new businesses. My commitment to Fremont is reflected in my extensive community leadership. I serve on the boards of the Ohlone College, Washington Health, and Fremont Education Foundations. Since my appointment to Fremont City Council in 2024, I have been committed to bringing our community together through meaningful conversations. I have made meaningful progress in addressing traffic issues, advocating for our unhoused neighbors, increasing support for local businesses, strengthening nonprofit partnerships, and enhancing public safety by working collaboratively to develop solutions that move the needle and reflect our community’s values and priorities. This has earned me the endorsement of elected officials including Congressmember Ro Khanna, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Assemblymember Alex Lee, all Mayors of the Tri-Cities, and many more. paragraphs: I have called Fremont home for more than two decades. I will bring an independent, evidence-based approach to public safety, homelessness, responsible budgeting, neighborhood quality of life, and Fremont’s future. I will not promise that every problem has a simple solution. I will promise to listen, prepare, explain my reasoning, and treat residents with respect, and pursue practical solutions. I spent more than 20 years in Silicon Valley as an engineer and technology entrepreneur before becoming a small business owner focused on community investment and development. Today, crime is down and we are recruiting and retaining good police officers. Housing is getting built for all income levels and new childcare providers, grocery stores, bakeries, and restaurants have expanded amenities in neighborhoods. Hayward continues to reduce homelessness by producing supportive housing and services. Education opportunities expanded to now include free transit passes for students, launched Hayward Rides to provide bicycles to students, and high school graduates now have guaranteed admission to Cal State East Bay. Looking ahead, my priorities are to make the City’s financial position stronger, reduce crime more, open more businesses and create jobs, and invest in safer streets for pedestrians, bicyclists, and drivers. Homeownership is a right, not a privilege — I’ll fight to create a direct pathway to homeownership for Hayward families, cutting through red tape and bureaucratic delays so more residents can finally own a piece of the city they call home. Hayward jobs should go to Hayward residents first, and I’ll push for hiring policies that prioritize our city’s workforce, so the opportunities we create stay right here and benefit the families who live here. Our seniors built this city with their hard work and sacrifice, and they shouldn’t be taxed out of the homes they’ve spent a lifetime paying for — I’ll champion no property tax for senior homeowners. Vote Brian Schott for strong leadership in District 1.

Renter protections are stronger, and we’ve built 500+ units of affordable, senior, and supportive housing. Fix the Downtown Loop to attract and support our local businesses. 3. Expand renter protections and affordable housing. 4. Improve public safety and wildfire preparedness. 5. Solve the structural budget deficit to restore social services. 6. Protect our environment from data centers. I am proud to be endorsed by over 60 organizations, local leaders, and elected officials. With your vote, we will continue to realize Hayward’s potential. Your friend, George Syrop.

While families are struggling with rising cost, a $5.5 million (460%) business license tax will be on our next ballot. A tax increase will ultimately be passed on to residents, cost jobs and harm our local economy. Please support my campaign for City Council. My campaign is focused on what matters most to our families and together, demand fiscal responsibility, support our public schools, support emergency services, and fix our roads. Please vote for Tonya Connolly.

My highest priority is to reallocate funds from our budget that I believe are spent in excess and put them towards a better quality of life. I believe in a future for Newark that supports everyone living and working in it, and if you believe the same, then I hope I can count on your support!

As a former Councilmember for nearly a decade, and now as a Zone 7 Water Agency Board Director, I have a proven track record of listening to everyone, presenting fresh, independent ideas, and building bridges to get things done. Pleasanton is taking steps to strengthen its financial future, and we must remain fiscally disciplined. We need leadership focused on fiscal responsibility, a stronger economy, transparency, and civic engagement to protect Pleasanton’s quality of life. I’m running a people-powered campaign because I believe the best ideas come from the people of Pleasanton, not just from City Hall. That’s why I’m making it easier for residents to stay informed, share ideas, and help shape decisions that affect our city. I’ll work alongside residents, businesses, city staff, and my fellow councilmembers to revitalize Downtown Pleasanton, support the redevelopment of Stoneridge Mall, attract businesses, reduce commercial vacancies, and grow the revenue base, not the tax rate. I support thoughtful housing, public safety, restoring library hours, and investing in infrastructure. In 1994, I purchased my first home to raise my family in the community I have always called home. Now, I am running to bring thoughtful leadership to City Council: supporting public safety, keeping our local economy strong and vibrant, fulfilling our infrastructure needs, and keeping City Hall transparent and accountable. For over 30 years, I have dedicated myself to public service and community leadership. Professionally, I have worked for Alameda County’s public health agency for 18 years, leading collaborations with local nonprofits, parent and community groups, and our schools, all to improve healthcare access for families and youth across our neighborhoods. With Pleasanton facing great challenges and greater opportunities, we deserve experienced, responsible leadership that learns from our past and plans for our future. I would be honored to serve. paragraphs: As Mayor, I’ve led with integrity, listened to our community, and delivered timely results. I initially helped City Council focus on strategic priorities, and by working together, we’ve made meaningful progress. For example, we’ve reduced crime, increased traffic enforcement, improved emergency response times, and expanded innovative behavioral health services. We’ve built more housing, strengthened renter protections, connected more unhoused residents with housing and support services, and made City Hall more responsive through improved communication and faster neighborhood problem-solving. We’ve also secured significant state and federal funding to improve our streets, expand library services, and invest in critical infrastructure while attracting clean energy, advanced manufacturing, and emerging technology companies that are creating new jobs and growing our local economy. Although we’ve made significant progress, our work is not finished. I remain committed to repairing aging infrastructure, completing projects on time and on budget, strengthening public safety, addressing homelessness with compassion and accountability, expanding housing opportunities, revitalizing our business community, and ensuring every neighborhood benefits from our progress. Together we have been building a Brighter Future for San Leandro. I respectfully ask for your vote so we can continue moving San Leandro forward in the right direction. SLMAY-1

San Leandro is a wonderful and diverse community, full of potential. But our city is becoming too costly. Everyday working families, seniors, and our own children cannot afford to live here. My name is James Maes, and I am running for Mayor to tackle this affordability crisis by making it easier to finally provide the housing and revenue we desperately need. I am a professional problem-solver. As a Business Operations Director and Chief of Staff for agencies like the U.S. Forest Service and Army Corps of Engineers, I have managed large budgets, built utilities and city facilities, led organizations, and negotiated labor agreements and contracts. Locally, I proudly serve as a Recreation and Parks Commissioner, a San Leandro High School coach, and past President of the Floresta Baseball League. Today, our city faces a difficult budget shortfall, and our local government has struggled to move forward together. We can do better. As Mayor, I won’t point fingers. Instead, I will use my real-world executive experience to unite our city council, resolve conflicts, and balance the budget without cutting the essential neighborhood services we need. Common Ground. More Housing. Lower Costs. I respectfully ask for your vote.

I’ve stayed rooted as former Chair of the Human Relations Commission, board member of Centro de Servicios, Union City Lions Club member, and volunteer in New Haven schools and at Our Lady of the Rosary parish. On the Council, I’ll fight to lower the cost of living, keep working families in their homes with real renter protections and affordable housing, expand public health and safety services, and protect immigrant families while ensuring they can access the resources they deserve. Looking ahead to the next four years, I remain committed to strengthening public safety, maintaining fiscal responsibility, investing in our neighborhoods, supporting local businesses, improving communication between City Hall and residents, and ensuring our local government remains transparent, responsive, and accountable. I am running for City Council to help bridge the gap between residents and their elected representatives by being accessible, approachable, and committed to effective communication and action! Since making Union City my home in 2021, my family and I have been proud to be part of this community while raising a child. I will leverage my 18+ years of technical and organizational experience at some of the top software companies of the country to bring the innovative, modern solutions needed to effectively implement this vision for our city’s bright future. I am committed to serving with integrity, working collaboratively, and ensuring every resident has a voice at City Hall. It would be an honor to earn your trust and your vote.

Born in the Philippines, I immigrated to the United States at a young age and have proudly called Union City home since 1977. As a caregiver for my autistic brother with Fragile X syndrome, a paraeducator in James Logan High School’s Adult Transition Program, a Chamber of Commerce member, and someone with a nursing background, I understand the challenges facing local families, seniors, individuals with disabilities, and businesses. My priorities are public safety, fiscal accountability, infrastructure, housing and homelessness solutions, and economic development. I will work for every neighbor regardless of political affiliation, religion, race, gender, or background. I believe Union City deserves leaders who listen, are accountable, and work together to find solutions while bridging communication between the City and residents. paragraphs: The quality of life in our neighborhoods is directly connected to the quality of our transit. For 25 years, I have lived in the East Bay, now raising a family. As chair of the Temescal/Telegraph BID Design and Economic Development committee, I advocated for the transportation, housing, and maintenance needs of the Temescal district. We need more buses, reliable connections with trains and ferries, and low-stress bike- and walk-ways accessible to all. I will fight to provide affordable and reliable transit so that we can all go to and from jobs, schools, shops, and medical care. Your representative on the AC Transit Board should bring deep empathy and transit experience to address the serious challenges facing AC Transit. Thank you for your vote.

Since joining the AC Transit Board, I have helped secure more than $1 million in funding for our hydrogen fuel cell bus program, voted to direct over $200 million in AC Transit contracting opportunities to local businesses that create and sustain good-paying jobs, and championed efforts to provide affordable, reliable, and expanded bus service for our communities. If elected, I will continue to advocate for: (1) keeping bus fares affordable for students, seniors, and individuals with disabilities; (2) increasing service throughout the AC Transit service area; and (3) investing in clean buses that protect our environment and public health. With 17 years of experience serving as an AC Transit Director, I am uniquely qualified to address the ongoing challenges facing AC Transit. I respectfully ask for your vote and invite you to join the coalition of bus drivers, riders, elected officials, and community leaders who are supporting my candidacy. It would be both an honor and a privilege to continue serving you and our community. For more information, please visit www.joelyoung.org.

This balanced management ensures our district remains transparent, responsive, and fiscally responsible while delivering exceptional value to our town. I am fully dedicated to protecting public health and our environment. I would be honored to have your support, and I respectfully ask for your vote.

paragraphs: I have served the Castro Valley Sanitary District for twenty six years and have helped guide the District on a course of responsible community service. I graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, am a Professional Civil Engineer and retired from the Alameda County Public Works Agency as Deputy Director of Public Works. My family and I have lived in Castro Valley for fifty years. My wife, Sherry, is retired from the Castro Valley Unified School District and both of our daughters graduated from Castro Valley High School.One daughter owns a small business (bakery) in Castro Valley. I am currently retired, so I have sufficient time to devote to the District’s management. My engineering background and management skills have helped me to actively participate on the Board and its committees. I sit on joint committees or Boards with the Oro Loma Sanitary District, East Bay Dischargers, Local Agency Formation Commission and the Alameda County Library Foundation. I have been able to work effectively with our Board members, staff, and the community to carry out the mission of the District, providing safe, low cost, and effective wastewater and solid waste management, while focusing on the best long term management of the District to preserve and enhance our investment in the sewage and solid waste systems.

I’m a resident of Castro Valley for nearly 50 years and a ratepayer of Castro Valley Sanitary District (CVSan). I’ve been married for over 50 years, have 3 grown children and 7 grandchildren. I am a retired sewer contractor with over 2,000 residential sewer replacements and a number of sewer mains in the Bay Area. It’s time for change. As a sewer contractor for over 30 years, I am highly qualified to sit on the CVSan Board. If elected I will push for term limits and paying off CVSan’s 30-year Bonds that cost the ratepayers around $1 Million per year for the new CVSan building. I started night law school at age 46 and received my Juris Doctor and LL.M. in environmental studies and passed the Bar on the first try, all while working full time as a sewer contractor. I have been involved with CVSan and have attended many Board and Committee meetings since 2010, either in person or by Zoom. I was responsible for drafting regulations with others for the “inspection upon sale” CVSan program. I personally was able to get the initial requirements more reasonable and manageable. Please vote for Ken Owen. www.Facebook/CvsanBoardElection/ CVSD-1

paragraphs: I’m running to ensure high quality service and the lowest responsible rates to EBMUD customers, using innovative approaches and in-house staff. I’ve worked in the municipal water treatment field since age 19, in plants across the US and in Kuwait, South Korea, and South Africa, and at EBMUD for 30+ years, most recently as Manager of Technical and Emerging Issues before retiring. I was a consultant and design engineer for EBMUD’s first major water recycling plant, which provides up to 5.4 million-gallons-daily. At EBMUD, I: worked with regulators to create regulations reducing treatment cost and your EBMUD bills; obtained 2 patents for first-of-their-kind processes to recycle food waste, otherwise landfilled, producing soil amendment and power for the electrical grid, and to operate infrastructure differently, lowering rates; secured grants from government and private organizations to conduct research that saved millions in both operating and capital costs; and developed use of existing facilities to meet new ammonia regulations, instead of spending $2B on new infrastructure that would have substantially raised rates. statement.designation: East Bay Municipal Utility District Director, Ward 3
paragraphs: When elected to EBMUD in 2014, I promised to expand water conservation and recycling, replace our aging pipelines, keep water affordable, lead on climate action, and protect the Mokelumne River. I kept those promises. I secured permanent protection of the Mokelumne and expanded watershed recreation access. I put EBMUD on a path to net zero emissions by 2030, prepared us for droughts, wildfires, and power shutoffs, and nearly tripled the pace of pipeline replacement to keep our water flowing 24/7/365. I drove our efforts to reduce harmful nutrients polluting the Bay. I made our shutoff moratorium permanent, and expanded our customer assistance program, ensuring no customer loses water due to inability to pay, while keeping rates affordable for everyone. I have spent more than 40 years in public service protecting our environment and improving the lives of working people, including as California Director of Clean Water Action, where I fought for safer drinking water and Bay Delta water quality. I am a third-generation Californian, lifelong EBMUD customer, and UC Berkeley graduate in Natural Resource Economics. My endorsements include EBMUD Directors, Clean Water Action, Sierra Club, AFSCME, and many other environmental, community, and labor leaders. statement.designation: Director,East Bay Municipal Utility District, Ward 7
paragraphs: Every dollar EBMUD spends matters. I treat your money as my money. As your EBMUD Director, I exposed $279 million in hidden budget transfers and led efforts to bring greater transparency and accountability to EBMUD’s finances. I advocated to eliminate the 8.5% drought surcharge in 2023 because Ward 7 families shouldn’t pay more than necessary. When a proposal threatened to turn Lake Chabot Road into a soil dump route with 100 trucks a day for 60 years, I stood with San Leandro and Castro Valley residents, and together we stopped it. As an Alameda County Fire Commissioner, I know public safety depends on reliable water. I initiated a new accountability standard for fire hydrant inspections because dependable hydrants save lives in wildfire-prone areas. The measure passed with support from the firefighters who rely on them. I’m not a career politician. I ask tough questions, challenge waste, and hold government accountable–even when it’s unpopular with insiders. If you want an independent voice who protects your dollars, stands up for our communities, and delivers results, I respectfully ask for your vote. Join Alameda County Supervisor Nate Miley, San Leandro Mayor Juan Gonzalez, and San Ramon Mayor Mark Armstrong in re-electing April Chan for EBMUD Ward 7 2026. https://chan4ebmud.com/ This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

I’m an expert, not a politician. I will bring my 40 years of experience as a water engineer and economist (wolff4water.org/about) to make the East Bay Municipal Utility District work better for you. I’ve been the Vice Chair of the California State Water Resources Control Board, the Executive Director of the Alameda County Waste Management Authority (“StopWaste”), a water and wastewater utility efficiency expert, a businessperson, and a licensed contractor. I’ve served on EBMUD and Castro Valley Sanitary District community advisory committees. I understand the problems we face, and I know that success requires listening and people skills, as well as technical knowledge. Water rates have gone up steeply, and climate change is affecting water quality. But we can keep water affordable, protect water quality, improve and expand the low-income customer assistance program, use water more efficiently, and keep parks and schools green. I will represent you as we build a better water future. That’s why more than 100 elected officials, community leaders, and organizations have endorsed me (wolff4water.org/endorsements). I humbly request your vote so that I may do this work for you. This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

As a Park Director, I will be a dedicated steward of our parks, committed to listening to the community, supporting park staff, and making responsible decisions. paragraphs: From Brushy Peak to Mission Peak, re-elect Olivia Sanwong for East Bay Regional Park District. I grew up participating in H.A.R.D. classes, recreation programs, and community activities that helped shape who I am today. I believe it’s time to invest in the next generation of leadership while honoring the strong foundation that has made H.A.R.D. an important part of our community. My experiences inspired my commitment to give back to the community that invested in me. Throughout my career, I have worked alongside CSU East Bay, Chabot College, UC Berkeley, UC San Diego, local businesses, and community organizations, managing budgets, building diverse teams, and collaborating with students, faculty, business executives, and community leaders to achieve shared goals and strengthen our communities. If elected, I will protect our parks and natural environment, preserve our community’s beauty, expand recreational opportunities, ensure residents of every age, ability, and background have access to H.A.R.D.’s programs and facilities, and build diverse, collaborative, and accessible teams. I believe every taxpayer deserves to know how their tax dollars are spent, and I will champion fiscal responsibility, transparency, and accountability. Please, District 4, I humbly ask for your vote for Joe Giltner for H.A.R.D. Director.

It has been a great honor to serve the H.A.R.D. Community as a member of the Board of Directors. I ask for your vote of confidence so I can continue to serve on the Board and support safe and accessible public parks while maintaining quality services that our community deserves, despite our current Statewide economic challenges. As a Hayward native, and a parent, teacher (at H.U.S.D), coach and businessman, I have always taken the proud position that H.A.R.D. is the ‘crown jewel’ of recreational and leisure centers throughout the Bay Area, thanks to our hard-working, loyal and caring staff, and your continued support and participation in H.A.R.D. activities. In this tight budget era, collaboration with other agencies is very important to create new projects and make capital improvements. I’m constantly networking with all government bodies and non-profit community-based groups in the H.A.R.D. footprint to obtain this goal. Please visit my website, www.hodges4hard.org, to learn more about the people who support me, my education, my wife and family, and our long-standing commitment to our community. I will continue my work to earn the trust you have placed in me by serving with honesty, integrity, openness and equality for all.
